name: Canals del Pedraforca
access: From Saldes follow the Pedraforca trail signs to the Font Teresana; park at the trailhead clearing below the canals and climb the north-face paths.
notes: The famous canals: steep, shady and heavily picked — be at the trailhead at dawn.

name: Obaga de Gresolet
access: Drive the Saldes-Gresolet road to the hamlet of Gresolet; park at the last houses and take the forest track north.
notes: Deep obaga on the Gresolet side; later fruiting than the canals and far quieter.

name: Serra de Padro (Bauma)
access: From the Saldes-Gósol road take the Bauma track at km 3 and drive to the clearing; the serra rises to the west.
notes: West-facing and drier; good second stop when the obagues are already picked.

name: Obaga de Feners
access: From Gósol take the road to Feners and park at the village; tracks climb into the north-facing pine belt.
notes: Quiet valley hamlet; the north slopes hold dew until midday.

name: Serra de Padro (oest)
access: Take the track west of Gósol toward the Padro ridge; park where the track forks at the coll.
notes: Long west flank with almost no competition on weekdays.

name: Plans de Gósol
access: Forest track leaving the Gósol-Saldes road eastwards at km 2; drivable to the plans.
notes: Higher east-facing benches; late-season producer.

name: Coll de Pal — obaga del Cadí
access: Park at the Coll de Pal pass; the black-pine belt spreads below the road on the Cadí side.
notes: High belt that switches on after the first cold nights; easy roadside access.

name: Baga de Maçaners
access: From Bagà take the Maçaners road to the hamlet; park at the chapel and follow the track into the baga.
notes: Classic shady slope between Bagà and the Cadí; reliable mid-season.

name: Penyes Altes nord
access: From the Maçaners track continue west to the foot of the Penyes Altes; leave the car at the barrier.
notes: Steeper and wilder; the north-west hollows keep the moss damp long after rain.

name: Obaga de Sant Quirc de Durban
access: From La Pobla take the Durban road to the Sant Quirc chapel; park at the chapel and walk the track behind it.
notes: Easy family obaga with a chapel landmark; moderate pressure on Sundays.

name: Pinedes sobre Asland
access: Park at the old Asland cement works and climb the track above the quarry.
notes: South-facing and early; rings first after the September storms.

name: Obaga del Llobregat
access: From La Pobla follow the Llobregat river track downstream for 2 km; park at the first ford.
notes: Riverside shade and humidity; undervalued corner.

name: Obaga del naixement del Llobregat
access: From Castellar follow the signs to the Llobregat springs; park at the picnic area and take the north track.
notes: Spray and shade around the springs; humid microclimate at the head of the valley.

name: Costa de llevant de Castellar
access: Forest track east of the village, at the first track signpost; drivable 1 km to the clearing.
notes: East benches warm early; good season opener.

name: Serra de Picancel
access: From Borredà take the track signposted to Picancel; park at the mas and continue on foot.
notes: Dissected serra between Borredà and La Quar; very low picker pressure.

name: Obaga nord de Borredà
access: From Borredà's church square take the cement track north for 800 m; park at the bend.
notes: Underrated pine flats; quick morning picks close to the road.

name: Canalda
area: La Coma i la Pedra · Port del Comte
access: From La Coma take the road to Canalda; park at the sanctuary and walk into the pines.
notes: The famous Canalda woods; big rings but expect company.

name: Obaga del Port del Comte
area: La Coma i la Pedra · Port del Comte
access: Take the Port del Comte road to the first ski-station bend; park at the lay-by and drop into the north slopes.
notes: Higher belt; best after the mid-October cold rains.

name: Obaga de Montgado
access: From Odèn follow the Cambrils road to the Montgado track fork; park at the cattle grid.
notes: Steep, silent valleys; some of the lowest picker pressure in the Solsonès.

name: Canalda — vessant oest
access: From the Canalda sanctuary continue on the ridge track west for 2 km; park at the next clearing.
notes: The quiet side of Canalda; same habitat, a fraction of the people.

name: Obaga de Sisquer
access: From Guixers take the road to Sisquer; park below the village and follow the track north.
notes: Vall de Lord benches with morning shade keeping the moss damp.

name: Serra de Busa
access: From Sant Llorenç de Morunys take the Busa road to the Hostal de Busa; park at the chapel and walk the serra.
notes: Cliff-top plateau; the damp hollows produce after light rains.

name: Obaga de la Vall de Lord
access: From Guixers take the old road along the reservoir; park at the second viaduct and climb north.
notes: Shaded slopes above the reservoir; afternoon shade holds humidity.

name: Obaga de Riard
access: From Solsona take the road to Riard; park at the hamlet and follow the track into the obaga.
notes: Close to town; go early on weekends or skip it.

name: Pinedes de Montclar
access: Take the Castell de Montclar road from Solsona's north exit; park at the castle track.
notes: Easy east benches; popular with Solsona locals.

name: Pinedes de Bergús
access: From Solsona take the Bergús road; park at the village and take the south-west track.
notes: Lower and drier; good after wet autumns.

name: Obaga de Madrona
access: From Castellar de la Ribera follow the Madrona signs; park at the hamlet and climb the track.
notes: North-west flank above the Ribera Salada; sleeps in until real rain arrives.

name: Pinedes de la Ribera Salada
access: Take the track along the Ribera Salada from the bridge; park at the picnic area.
notes: Riverside pines; the river humidity helps after dry weeks.

name: Obaga d'Anserall
access: From La Seu take the Anserall road; park at the Valira confluence bridge and take the north track.
notes: North slopes of the Valira; easy half-day trip from town.

name: Costa de Castellciutat
access: Drive up to Castellciutat and park at the viewpoint; the pines stretch south below the crag.
notes: South-facing and early; rings with the first September storms.

name: Obaga nord de la Seu
access: From the north side of town take the farm track towards the hills; park at the first bend.
notes: Backyard woods of La Seu; surprisingly decent after October rains.

name: Obaga d'Organyà
access: From Organyà take the road toward Fígols; park at the first hairpin and climb north.
notes: Peramola range pines; needs a wet autumn to deliver.

name: Solà d'Organyà
access: Take the track south of the village past the water tank; drivable to the solà.
notes: South face: only worth it after heavy autumn rains.

name: Obaga de Peramola
access: From Peramola take the track toward Tragó; park at the pass and walk west.
notes: Dissected terrain with very low picker pressure.

name: Costa de Tragó
access: Continue on the Tragó road to the abandoned village; park below it.
notes: East terraces over the Segre; almost unknown to pickers.

name: Obaga de Coll de Nargó
access: From Coll de Nargó cross the Fígol river and climb the west track; park at the transformer hut.
notes: Quiet foothills along the Fígol; check the shaded cuts.

name: Pinedes de Gavarra
access: Take the road to Gavarra; park at the village and enter the pines east.
notes: Abandoned-farmland pines; a mosaic of clearings and thickets.

name: Obaga de la Vall de Castellbò
access: From La Seu take the Castellbò road to the village; park at the castle ruin and follow the north track.
notes: Border valley, damp and rarely crowded.

name: Muntanya de Montferrer
access: From Montferrer village take the track up the mountain; park at the spring.
notes: North-west hollows catch the damp air coming off the Cerdanya.

name: Obaga de Sant Cristòfol
access: From Campdevànol take the road up to Sant Cristòfol; park at the church and walk the track behind it.
notes: Convenient from the C-17; early birds win here.

name: Pinedes de la Ruta del Ferro
access: Park at the Ruta del Ferro trailhead on the C-17 and follow the interpretation path up.
notes: Family-friendly old mining tracks; picked near the path, better further in.

name: Obaga nord de Campdevànol
access: From town take the forest track opposite the campsite; park at the gate after 1 km.
notes: Continuous pine north of town; holds moisture well.

name: Puig Estela nord
access: From Ogassa follow the old miners' track toward Puig Estela; park at the pass and climb north.
notes: The north face under Puig Estela keeps the moss wet; continuous forest.

name: Vessant est d'Ogassa
access: From Ogassa village take the east track past the last mas; park at the barrier.
notes: East terraces; rings early in the season.

name: Obaga del Freser
access: From Queralbs follow the Núria road to the first tunnel; park at the lay-by and take the west path.
notes: High valley of the Freser; peaks around late October.

name: Pinedes del camí de Núria
access: Continue on the Núria road to the hairpins above Queralbs; park at the second bend and enter the pines north.
notes: Cold and shaded; good in mild Novembers.

name: Camí de Coma de Vaca
access: From the Núria road take the Coma de Vaca trail signpost; the lower pine belt starts at the trail gate.
notes: Long walk in, but essentially untouched ground.

name: Pinedes de Surroca
access: From Sant Joan take the Surroca road; park at the old mines and walk east.
notes: East-facing terraces warm up early in the season.

name: Obaga del Bac
access: Take the road toward el Bac; park at the farm and follow the shady track north.
notes: Shady pocket valley between Sant Joan and Ogassa.

name: Obaga de Vallfogona
access: From Vallfogona take the track behind the church northwards; park at the first gate.
notes: Rolling farmland-pine mosaic; check the north hedge lines.

name: Serrat de Vallfogona
access: From the valley road take the serra track; park at the communications tower.
notes: Open crest with scattered pines; early fruiting on the warm side.

name: Obaga de Planoles
access: From Planoles take the forest road north of the village; park at the water deposit and walk in.
notes: Cool and shaded; good in mild Novembers.

name: Vessant est de Planoles
access: Take the farm track opposite the N-260 bend; park at the barn.
notes: East slopes with continuous canopy toward the Tossa zone.

name: Volcà de Santa Margarida
access: From Santa Pau follow the Garrotxa volcanoes trail to the Santa Margarida car park; the pine belt circles the crater.
notes: Pine patches between the volcanoes, mixed with chestnut; easy walking.

name: Costa de la Vall de Bianya
access: From the Santa Pau-Bianya road park at Els Hostalets and take the track east.
notes: Humid valley with a pine-chestnut mix; low pressure on weekdays.

name: Obaga del castell de Finestres
access: From Sant Aniol follow the track to the Finestres castle; park below the crag and walk the north path.
notes: Finestres castle slopes; surprise producer after storms.

name: Costa de Sant Miquel
access: Continue past the castle track to the Sant Miquel fork; park at the col.
notes: Warmer south-west face; earliest fruiting of the zone.

name: Puig de Bastiments
access: From Les Preses take the Bastiments track; park at the farm gate and climb the north path.
notes: A proper hill obaga next to the flat family woods near Olot.

name: Costa de Bellpuig
access: From Les Preses follow the Bellpuig signs; park at the hermitage clearing.
notes: South-east face above the valley floor; dries fast — go right after rain.

name: Obaga de Mieres
access: From Mieres take the track north past the church; park at the bend.
notes: Warm, early zone; check the humid gullies.

name: Solà de Mieres
access: From the village square take the south track to the solà; park at the hut.
notes: Only productive in wet autumns; good views regardless.

name: Costes de Sant Privat
access: From Sant Privat d'en Bas take the track behind the church; park at the bridge.
notes: West rim of the valley; afternoon shade after a morning elsewhere.

name: Obaga sobre Els Hostalets
access: From Els Hostalets d'en Bas take the north track past the last houses.
notes: Humid corner under the cliff rim; steady if unspectacular.

name: Sant Sebastià de Viladrau
access: From Viladrau take the Sant Sebastià road to the hermitage; park at the spring and walk the north track.
notes: The Montseny classic; very popular — be there at dawn.

name: Pinedes de la Font Trobada
access: From the Sant Sebastià road continue to the Font Trobada fork; park at the picnic tables.
notes: Deep shady pinewood; dew holds until midday.

name: Pla de la Calma
access: Take the track to the Pla de la Calma; leave the car at the gate before the pla and walk in.
notes: High meadows ringed by pine; late season and low pressure.

name: Obaga d'Espinelves
access: From Espinelves take the Arbreda road to the last mas; park at the track barrier.
notes: Fira de l'Arbreda crowds in November; walk further in than they do.

name: Torrent d'Espinelves
access: Follow the stream track below the village; park where the track narrows.
notes: Shady streamside pines; the fair crowds never come this far.

name: Pinedes del camí de Viladrau
access: From Espinelves take the Viladrau track; park at the mas gate and continue on foot.
notes: Woods straddling the Espinelves-Viladrau boundary; deep and shaded.

name: Sant Miquel de Solterra
access: From Sant Hilari take the Solterra road to the castle ruin; park at the track end.
notes: Guilleries high ground with extensive pine tracts.

name: La Gutina
access: Take the road to the La Gutina pass; park at the pass and enter the pines east.
notes: Pass forest that catches the morning fog moisture.

name: Vall d'Osor
access: From Sant Hilari take the Osor road; park at the reservoir bridge and climb west.
notes: West slopes above the Osor reservoir; humid and green.

name: Sant Corneli de Tavertet
access: From Tavertet follow the Sant Corneli signs; park at the hermitage and walk the south path.
notes: Clifftop pines over the Ter; drier south faces.

name: Obaga del Cingle de Tavertet
access: Take the road toward L'Avenc and park at the bend; the obaga drops north.
notes: North side of the cliff; the valley humidity climbs up at dusk.

name: Obaga de Pruit
access: From Rupit take the Pruit road to the hamlet; park at the church and follow the track north-west.
notes: Rupit itself is picked over; the Pruit side is quieter.

name: Obaga del Salt de Sallent
access: From Rupit follow the Salt de Sallent path; park at the picnic area before the descent.
notes: Spray from the falls keeps the obaga damp; steep ground.

name: Costa de Fontmartina
access: From Montseny village take the Fontmartina road to the farmhouse; park at the track fork.
notes: Deep Montseny; track access only, worth the walk.

name: Camí de Sant Segimon
access: From Fontmartina follow the Sant Segimon trail signposts; the pine belt starts above the chestnuts.
notes: Long climb to the chapel saddle; untouched north-west hollows.

name: Obaga de Naens
access: From Senterada take the Naens road to the hamlet; park at the last house and climb north.
notes: Bòvida valley pines; zero crowds.

name: Pinedes de Cérvoles
access: Continue on the Cérvoles road; park below the village and enter the east pines.
notes: Abandoned terraces gone to pine; humid pockets in the cuts.

name: Obaga de Montsor
access: From La Pobla cross the Segre to Montsor; park at the village and take the west track.
notes: Shady flank over the Segre; mid-season sweet spot.

name: Costa de Sant Miquel del Pui
access: Take the road up to Sant Miquel del Pui; park at the chapel.
notes: Sunny confluence of the Flamisell and Segre; early ring.

name: Obaga de Talarn
access: From Talarn take the track to the reservoir viewpoint; park at the bend and drop north.
notes: Dry zone: only worth it after heavy autumn rains.

name: Solà de Talarn
access: From the village take the south track past the olive terraces.
notes: Mediterranean face; a gamble except in wet autumns.

name: Obaga de Salàs
access: From Salàs follow the reservoir road; park at the second bend and climb west.
notes: Overlooked woods above the reservoir.

name: Costa est de Salàs
access: From the village take the east track to the antenna; park below it.
notes: Morning sun; go right after rain.

name: Obaga de Llessui
access: From Sort take the Llessui road to the village; park at the small resort base and walk north.
notes: Wide high obaga; cold nights concentrate the fruiting.

name: Pinedes de Bernui
access: From the Sort-Gerri road take the Bernui turn; park at the hamlet.
notes: Easy east benches; rings early in September.

name: Vall d'Àssua
access: From Sort cross to the Vall d'Àssua road; park at Altron and take the south-east track.
notes: Quiet side valley; terraced pines above the fields.

name: Obaga de Burgo
access: From Esterri take the Burgo road; park at the hamlet and follow the north track.
notes: Àneu valley shade; cold nights bring on the flush.

name: Muntanya d'Arcalís
access: From Esterri take the Unarre road to the Arcalís track fork; park at the gate.
notes: North-east flanks of Arcalís; wild and productive.

name: Obaga d'Isil
access: From Esterri take the Isil road; park at the village entrance and follow the north track.
notes: Upper Noguera shade; a cold-weather producer.

name: Obaga de Bonabé
access: From Alt Àneu take the Bonabé track; park at the shepherd's hut and climb north-west.
notes: High Bonabé forests; the season ends early here.

name: Vessant sud de la Bonaigua
access: Take the C-28 toward the Bonaigua pass; park at the first hairpin below the pass and drop north.
notes: Black-pine belt under the pass; late-season gold.

name: Serra de Mossers
access: From Bellver take the Mossers road to the serra track; park at the cattle grid.
notes: Sunny Cerdanya shoulder; best after the September storms.

name: Pinedes de Talltendre
access: Take the Talltendre road and park at the village; tracks run east into the pines.
notes: High benches; cold nights, slow but steady fruiting.

name: Costa de Nas
access: From Bellver take the Nas road to the hamlet; park at the church and walk west.
notes: Overlooked western flank toward the Segre gorge.

name: Obaga de la Tosa d'Alp
access: From Alp take the track toward La Tosa; park at the fountain below the ski slopes and climb north.
notes: North faces toward Tosa d'Alp; late-season stronghold.

name: Bosc de Masella
access: From the Masella base station follow the summer trail under the lifts; park at the resort.
notes: Pines between the ski runs; productive strips everyone misses.

name: La Molosa
access: From Alp take the La Molosa track; park at the farm and enter the east pines.
notes: Quiet east flank between Alp and Das.

name: Els Mosolls
access: From Das take the Mosoll road; park at the hamlet and walk east.
notes: Quiet municipal forests.

name: Obaga de Das
access: From the village take the north track past the water tank; park at the bend.
notes: Small north pocket; holds dew after drizzle.

name: Pinedes d'Olopte
access: From Isòvol cross to Olopte; park at the village and take the east track.
notes: East terraces that catch the afternoon storms.

name: Obaga d'Isòvol
access: From the village take the west track above the fields; park at the shed.
notes: West slopes above the Cerdanya floor; check after storm days.

name: Serra de Pinós — obaga
access: From the Pinós shrine take the north track; park at the picnic area.
notes: The shady side of Pinós; much better than the sunny face.

name: Pinedes del Salí
access: From the Cardona salt-mountain road park at the Salí gate; tracks run west.
notes: Pines over the salt valley; the fast-draining soil needs solid rain first.

name: Pinedes de Serrateix
access: From Cardona take the Serrateix road; park at the monastery and walk south-east.
notes: Monastery woods; moderate pressure and a nice pine-oak mix.

name: Cingles de Bertí
access: From Moià take the Sant Quirze Safaja road; park at the Bertí track fork and walk to the cliff edge.
notes: Cliff-top pines; the shade line along the cingle is the productive strip.

name: Obaga de Moià
access: From Moià take the Granera road; park at the first track heading north.
notes: Central Moianès plateau; quick from Barcelona but picked early.

name: El Sot de Moià
access: Take the track south-west of town past the sports field; park at the stream crossing.
notes: Sheltered hollow; keeps humidity after dry spells.

name: Coll de Collsuspina
access: Park at the pass on the C-59; the tracks drop north into the shade.
notes: Shady pass forests; good moisture retention.

name: Costa de llevant de Collsuspina
access: From the pass take the east track past the antenna; park at the gate.
notes: East slopes toward l'Esquirol; a morning-light ring walk.

name: Obaga de Prats de Lluçanès
access: From Prats de Lluçanès take the track behind the church; park at the sports field and walk north-west.
notes: Lluçanès plateau woods; quiet, central and overlooked.

name: Pinedes de Santa Coloma Sasserra
access: From the Moià-Granera road take the Santa Coloma turn; park at the church and follow the north track.
notes: Small serra with healthy pine and almost no pickers.

name: Obaga del camí de Fonollosa
access: From Sant Fruitós take the Fonollosa road; park at the track fork after 2 km.
notes: Low Aleppo stands; early and late-season trickles.

name: Pinedes del pla de Bages
access: From the Santpedor road take the vineyard track; park at the irrigation pond.
notes: Hot pine-and-vineyard mosaic; only for early-season scouts.

name: La Mola — obaga
access: From Sant Llorenç Savall take the trail to La Mola; park at the trailhead past the village and climb to the monastery saddle.
notes: Closest to Barcelona and heavily picked — walk past the monastery for unpicked strips.

name: Vall d'Horta
access: Take the Horta valley road; park at the casal and follow the track east.
notes: Sheltered valley; locals start here at first light.

name: Serrat de la Bauma
access: From the western exit of the village take the serra track; park at the bend.
notes: South face; only after a wet week, then surprisingly good.

name: Sant Pere de Gallifa
access: From Gallifa follow the Sant Pere signs; park at the church and take the north path.
notes: Small-village forest tracks; moderate pressure.

name: Costa de Gallifa
access: From the pass road take the south track; park at the farm gate.
notes: Sunny side; pairs with the obaga as an early/late option.

name: El Tagamanent
access: From Tagamanent village take the hill road; park below the church on the summit.
notes: Montseny southern gateway; quiet on weekdays.

name: Obaga sud del Montseny
access: From the same road take the north-facing track at the fountain; park at the bend.
notes: First shady slopes of the Montseny massif coming up from the south.

name: Bosc Vell de Poblet
access: From the Poblet monastery follow the forest track north; park at the barrier past the sports field.
notes: Poblet forests; a classic family outing — walk past the first kilometre.

name: Pinedes de la Pena
access: Take the la Pena turn from the main road; park at the village and walk west.
notes: West flank above the Pena stream; mid-level pressure.

name: Costa de Montblanquet
access: From the Poblet road take the Montblanquet track; park at the hamlet.
notes: Tiny hamlet with pine benches; almost nobody bothers.

name: Camí Milà i Fontanals
access: From l'Espluga follow the Milà i Fontanals trail signs; park at the fountain at the town edge.
notes: Interpretation trail through Aleppo pine; family-scale pickings.

name: Vessant est de Poblet
access: From the road to Poblet park at the first bend past the town; climb the north track.
notes: Lower Poblet shade; better than the Espluga floor.

name: Tossal de la Baltasana
access: From Prades take the track to the tossal; park at the track end below the summit.
notes: Top rovelló fame — and crowds; walk the north drop from the summit.

name: Obaga de la Farena
access: From Capafonts take the Farena road; park above the village and descend into the obaga.
notes: Steep shaded valley; the further from the road, the better.

name: Pinedes d'Albarca
access: From the Prades-Albarca road park at the hamlet; tracks climb north-west.
notes: North-west benches near the abandoned village; strong habitat, low pressure.

name: Obaga de Capafonts
access: From Capafonts take the track behind the last houses; park at the spring.
notes: Prades' quieter eastern flank; good dew catch.

name: Camí de Mont-ral
access: Take the Mont-ral track; park at the pass above the Brugent gorge.
notes: East slopes over the Brugent gorge; humid air climbs from the stream.

name: Serra del Gaià — vessant sud-oest
access: From Aiguamúrcia take the Gaià ridge track; park at the tower.
notes: Gaià range; humid pockets after the rains.

name: Pinedes de Santes Creus
access: From the Santes Creus monastery take the track past the mill; park at the picnic area.
notes: Riverside pines on the Gaià headwaters; early trickle.

name: Obaga de la Morera
access: From La Morera take the Escaladei road; park at the first bend and climb north-west.
notes: Montsant canyon rim; pine and holm-oak mix.

name: Costa d'Escaladei
access: From La Morera continue to Escaladei; park at the old charterhouse and take the east track.
notes: Shaded terraces of the Priorat; a vineyard-pine mosaic.

name: Costa de la Figuera
access: From La Figuera take the track toward the Montsant cliff; park at the vineyard shed.
notes: South rim above the Ebro; earliest of the Montsant sectors.

name: Costers d'Àger
access: From Àger take the Corçà road; park at the hamlet and climb the south track.
notes: Dry Montsec south faces; only in wet years.

name: Obaga del Montsec d'Àger
access: From the Àger-Os de Balaguer road take the first forest track north; park at the bend.
notes: North face of the Montsec; surprisingly better after storm weeks.

name: Obaga de la Sarga
access: From Camarasa cross the Segre toward la Sarga; park at the village and climb west.
notes: Congost approaches; a shaded strip along the reservoir.

name: Obaga del congost
access: From the Fontllonga road park at the track to the Mont-rebei path.
notes: Cliff shade by the Segre gorge; humidity pockets only.

name: Obaga dels Ports
access: From Horta take the road toward Els Ports; park at the barrier before the park boundary and climb north.
notes: Els Ports north faces; rovellons with mountain sage.

name: Pinedes de Santa Bàrbara
access: From the Horta-Santa Bàrbara road park at the wind-farm track; walk east.
notes: East terraces between olives and pine; storm-fed.

name: Barranc de la Vall Major
access: From Horta take the Vall Major track; park at the second ford and climb north-west.
notes: Deep shady barranc; the Ports humidity pools here.

name: Obaga d'Arnes
access: From Arnes take the track toward the Ports; park at the fire tower and walk north-west.
notes: Ports foothills; wet autumns are a bonus.

name: Vessant est d'Arnes
access: From the village take the east track past the olive mill; park at the bend.
notes: Morning-sun sector; go right after the first autumn storm.

name: Tossal d'en Cama — obaga
access: From La Sénia take the Godall road; park at the tossal track and climb north.
notes: Southernmost pine mix; only after wet October weeks.

name: Pinedes de Godall
access: From Godall village take the north track; park at the water tank.
notes: Plateau pines with a sea-humidity drift at night.

name: Serra de Llaberia — obaga
access: From the coll de Llaberia take the track to the antenna; park below the summit.
notes: Coastal-range pines; night humidity drifts in from the sea.

name: Costa del coll de Llaberia
access: From the coast road take the Llaberia pass; park at the col and walk east.
notes: East face; the sea fog does the watering.

name: Obaga de Costabona
access: From Setcases take the Vallter road to the last bend below the station; park at the lay-by and climb the Costabona tracks into the north face.
notes: The great shady wall above the Ter headwaters; big rings after October storms, but a long climb.

name: Pinedes del Ter (Setcases)
access: From Setcases follow the Vallter road 4 km; park at the Font del Faig lay-by and take the track north-east above the river.
notes: Black-pine belt that holds dew until noon; classic mid-season stop.

name: Serra del Cim
access: From the Vallter road take the Cim track signpost; leave the car at the barrier and follow the ridge path north-west.
notes: High west flank; switches on late in the season after the first frosts.

name: Obaga de Beget
access: From Camprodon take the Beget road to the last bend above the village; park at the bridge and follow the forest track north.
notes: Steep quiet obaga above the stone village; very low weekend pressure.

name: Obaga de Rocabruna
access: From Camprodon take the road to Rocabruna; park at the village and climb the track behind the church.
notes: Sunny-side hamlet with a shady back slope; rings early after September rain.

name: Obaga de Montgrony
access: From Gombreny follow the signs to the Montgrony sanctuary; park at the sanctuary and take the track below the cliffs.
notes: The north wall under the Montgrony cliffs; damp moss and big rings, some company on Sundays.

name: Serra de Montgrony (oest)
access: From the Montgrony track continue west along the serra; park at the first cattle grid and walk the ridge path.
notes: Long west flank above the Llobregat forks; almost nobody on weekdays.

name: Obaga de Catllaràs
access: From Guardiola take the road toward Sant Jaume de Frontanyà; at the Pendís fork park at the clearing and climb the track north.
notes: The whole hidden massif between the Llobregat and Merdès valleys; reliable and quiet.

name: Serrat de Catllaràs (llevant)
access: From Guardiola follow the La Pobla road to the Sant Jaume turn; park at the second bend and take the east track.
notes: East benches below the Catllaràs antenna; a good second lap after the obaga.

name: Obaga dels Rasos de Peguera
access: From Berga take the Rasos de Peguera road to the ski station; park at the station and walk straight into the north slopes.
notes: Berga's backyard: road-accessible high obaga, so expect pickers — go on a weekday morning.

name: Serrat de la Bòfia
access: From the Rasos road take the Bòfia forest track at km 6; drivable to the barrier, then walk north-west.
notes: Quiet north-west serrat below the Rasos; the name says where the humidity collects.

name: Coma dels Rasos
access: From the ski station take the eastward cross-country track; park where it forks at the first clearing.
notes: East-facing bowl that thaws first; good early-season producer.

name: Obaga de l'Ensija
access: From Vallcebre take the Ensija gravel road to the clearing above the quarries; park at the barrier and climb into the north belt.
notes: High black-pine wall of the Ensija; late-season gold after the first cold nights.

name: Ensija — vessant de Saldes
access: From Saldes take the Ensija road past the Feners turn; park at the second cattle grid and drop into the north-west hollows.
notes: The Saldes side of the serra; silent and steep, keeps humidity for days after rain.

name: Puigllançada — obaga major
access: From the Coll de Pal road park at the Puigllançada signpost; climb the track into the north slopes below the summit.
notes: Big black-pine bowl between Bagà and La Pobla; rings well into November.

name: Puigllançada — serrat est
access: From the Coll de Pal road take the first forest track east; park at the bend and follow the serrat crest.
notes: East spur of Puigllançada; dries out sooner — start the season here.

name: Obaga de la Vansa
access: From the La Vansa hamlet follow the valley track toward the Port del Comte side; park at the barrier beyond the last mas.
notes: The valley nobody drives through; dense pine and some of the lowest pressure in the Alt Urgell.

name: Obaga de Josa
access: From Josa village take the track behind the church; park at the fold and climb north-east.
notes: Tiny walled village, huge quiet forest; a local secret.

name: Costa de Tuixén
access: From Tuixén take the Josa road out of the village; park at the first bend and climb west.
notes: West-facing benches above Tuixén; the afternoon-warm option of the valley.

name: Obaga d'Espot
access: From Espot take the Sant Maurici road to the first hairpin; park at the lay-by and take the north track away from the park boundary.
notes: Stay outside the Aigüestortes boundary — collecting inside the national park is not allowed.

name: Obaga de Gerri
access: From Gerri cross the bridge and take the forest track on the right; park after the water tank and climb north.
notes: Shady wall above the salt-town; monastery-hamlet start to the morning.

name: Obaga de la Vall Fosca
area: La Torre de Cabdella · Vall Fosca
access: From La Torre follow the road up the Fosca valley to the Cabdella power station; park at the bend before the tunnels and take the north track.
notes: The 'dark valley' earns its name: north slopes that stay damp all October.

name: Montsent de Pallars nord
area: La Torre de Cabdella · Vall Fosca
access: From Mont-ros take the track toward the Montsent antenna; park at the saddle and follow the north-west path.
notes: The lone giant between the Fosca and Flamicell; wind-swept but the hollows produce.

name: Obaga de Lles
access: From Lles take the forest road toward Aransa; park at the first bend and walk into the north belt.
notes: Cerdanya's easy high obaga; popular with Andorra day-trippers, go early.

name: Cap del Rec — obaga
access: Forest road from Lles to the Cap del Rec refuge; park at the refuge and take the tracks north of it.
notes: High refuge plateau; late-season producer that keeps fruiting into December.

name: Obaga de Meranges
access: From Meranges follow the road toward the Engorgs valley; park where it turns to track and walk into the north-east pines.
notes: Border-valley black pine; quiet and cold, later fruiting than the Cerdanya floor.

name: Bosc de Guils
access: From Guils take the track behind the village toward the border; park at the barrier and walk north into the pines.
notes: Big flat Scots-pine wood on the valley floor; classic family forest, busy on Sundays.

name: Serra de Guils
access: From the Guils road take the track west at the church; park at the fold and climb the serra.
notes: West-facing shoulder above the village; drier than the bosc but productive after wet weeks.

name: Pinedes de Queixans
access: From Queixans take the track behind the houses; park at the last barn and climb north-east.
notes: Sheltered north-east pines below the village; holds moisture late into the season.

name: Obaga de Fontanals
access: From Fontanals de Cerdanya take the track north of the station; park at the first bend.
notes: Working forest with tracks and clearings; check the northern edge where it stays damp.

name: Obaga d'Urús
access: From Urús take the only road out of the village north; park where the tarmac ends and continue on foot.
notes: Compact north slope above the tiny village; overlooked by the ski crowds heading to Masella.

name: Obaga de Montellà
access: From Montellà take the track toward the Cadí; park at the last mas and climb north.
notes: First Cadí north faces above the Cerdanya floor; mixes Scots and black pine as it climbs.

name: Baga de Martinet
access: From Martinet cross the river and take the track up the west side; park at the first bend.
notes: North-west baga at the mouth of the valley; good early-season option when the high zones are dry.

name: Serrat de Ger
access: From Ger take the Puigcerdà road and turn onto the serrat track; park at the water tank.
notes: Open Scots-pine serrat east of the village; quiet corner rarely visited by pickers.

name: Obaga de Prullans
access: From Prullans take the road toward Ardòvol; park at the fold and climb into the pines.
notes: Damp north belt between Prullans and the Berenguers range; reliable after October rains.

name: Serrat de les Esposes
access: From Riu de Cerdanya follow the semi-paved track toward Coll de Pendís for 6 km; park at the refuge clearing on the pla de les Esposes and work the belts around it.
notes: Big Moixeró north face inside the Cadí-Moixeró park; spectacular fir-and-pine obaga on the Cavalls del Vent trail — go early, hikers and pickers share it.

name: Camí del Coll de Pendís
access: Continue past the Serrat de les Esposes refuge up to the parking barrier below the coll; the black-pine slopes stretch either side of the fence.
notes: High pass woodland on the Cerdanya-Berguedà fence; late fruiting, often good in November once the valley pines are done.

name: Pinedes de Riu
access: From Riu de Cerdanya take the Pedra road west; park at the first fold and climb the south-west pines above the village.
notes: Sunny Scots-pine belt above the Cadí tunnel service area; warms up first — a good early-season check before heading up the obaga.

name: Obaga de Montnegre
access: From Fogars de Montclús take the road over the Montnegre ridge; park at the track junction below the summit and drop into the north slopes toward Tordera.
notes: Aleppo-pine rovellons 40 minutes from the coast; busy on Maresme Sundays.

name: Obaga de Sant Iscle
access: From Sant Iscle de Vallalta follow the valley track; park at the water tank and walk up the north-east slopes.
notes: Sea-humidity drift makes this the first Aleppo belt to fruit after August storms.

name: Obaga d'Osor
access: From Osor take the Anglès road 2 km; park at the reservoir track and climb north into the Guilleries.
notes: Deep Guilleries obaga; damp valley granite that holds water all season.

name: Obaga del Ter (Osor)
access: From Osor take the Susqueda road to the first ford; park at the bend and follow the river-side track north.
notes: Low humid belt by the Ter; early producer before the high forests wake.

name: Obaga de Sant Feliu
area: Sant Feliu de Pallerols · Vall d'Hostoles
access: From Sant Feliu de Pallerols take the road toward les Planes; park at the first bridge and follow the track north-east.
notes: Southern gateway to the Garrotxa pines; quiet and family-friendly.

name: Obaga del Cogolls
area: Sant Feliu de Pallerols · Vall d'Hostoles
access: From El Cogolls hamlet take the track behind the houses; park at the last barn and climb north.
notes: Hidden hamlet under the Sant Miquel slopes; some of the biggest rings of the comarca.

name: L'Obac de Mura
access: From Mura take the Talamanca road to the l'Obac information point; park there and take the north-west paths.
notes: The massif literally named 'the shady side'; close to Barcelona so dawn is essential.

name: Obaga de Mura
access: From Mura's plaça take the cement track north; park at the bend by the stream and climb into the pines.
notes: Stream-side Aleppo belt; fruits after any decent September storm.

name: Serra del Montcau — obaga
access: From Talamanca take the road to the Coll d'Estenalles; park at the information centre and follow the Montcau path north.
notes: The park's high north-west corner; cooler and later than the Mura slopes.

name: Obaga de Requesens
access: From La Jonquera take the Requesens castle track (gravel, drivable); park below the castle and walk into the north slopes.
notes: Castle-crowd slopes on the French border; the north face is the productive side.

name: Pinedes de Capmany
access: From Capmany take the Requesens track 3 km; park at the fold and climb the north-east slopes.
notes: Wine-village pines; the tramuntana dries them fast, go right after rain.

name: Obaga de les Salines
access: From Maçanet take the road to the Salines sanctuary; park at the sanctuary and take the north tracks.
notes: Sanctuary forest on the French border; mixed pine with a damp north face.

name: Serra de les Salines — vessant est
access: Beyond the sanctuary continue on the ridge track; park at the fold and walk the east slopes.
notes: Far side of the serra; almost zero pressure, fruits after southern rains.

name: Obaga del Montsec (Sant Esteve)
area: Sant Esteve de la Sarga · Montsec
access: From Sant Esteve take the road to la Clua; park at the hamlet and follow the track toward the crest on the north face.
notes: The great north wall of the Montsec; rovellóns with a view down the whole Noguera.

name: Obaga d'Alsamora
area: Sant Esteve de la Sarga · Montsec
access: From Alsamora hamlet take the track north-west; park at the last house and climb the hollow.
notes: Terraced-world hamlet above the Mont-rebei gorge; quiet and damp.

name: Obaga de Llaberia
access: From Pradell take the Coll de Julià road to Llaberia village; park at the church and take the track north.
notes: The real Llaberia heartland: north face, Priorat quiet, big rings after October rain.

name: Costa del Coll de Julià
access: From Pradell park at the Coll de Julià pass; walk the north-east slopes below the antennas.
notes: Pass-side belt that catches both sea fog and inland rain.

name: Obaga de Fontmartina
access: From Sant Esteve de Palautordera take the Fontmartina track; park at the mas and climb north toward the Turó de l'Home belt.
notes: The west-Montseny Scots belt; the Vallès classic, busy on Sundays.

name: Obaga de Mosqueroles
access: From Mosqueroles take the track above the houses; park at the fold and climb the north-east slopes.
notes: Lower and earlier than Fontmartina; good opener while the high belt is still dry.

name: Obaga de Ciuret
access: From Vidrà take the road to Ciuret; park at the hamlet and follow the track north into the pine belt.
notes: Border-of-three-comarques forest; dense, quiet, and famously productive.

name: Obaga de Sant Segimon
access: From Vidrà take the Sant Segimon road to the shrine; park at the saddle and drop into the north hollows.
notes: Shrine-side obaga between Vidrà and el Brull; damp hollows that fruit long.

name: Pinedes de Montcorbuda
access: From Vielha take the track signposted for Montcorbuda at the north end of town; park at the first clearing by the water tank.
notes: Shady strips above the village that hold dew well, but local pickers work them hard — go at dawn.

name: Solana de Casau
access: From Vielha take the road through Escunhau to Casau; park at the upper edge of the village where the track onto the solana begins.
notes: A warm, early bank that dries out fast after rain, so it only fruits properly in wet autumns.

name: Boscs d'Escunhau
access: From Vielha take the road to Escunhau; park at the last barns and follow the track onto the north-east flank above the village.
notes: A dependable mid-height belt between the valley floor and the high canals, steady from late September in wet years.

name: Era Artiga de Lin
access: From Salardú take the Valarties road up to Era Artiga de Lin; park at the barriers by the meadow huts.
notes: A high black-pine belt that only gets going in October and keeps its moisture well into November.

name: Pòrt de Caldes
access: From Era Artiga de Lin follow the Colomèrs trail up the Valarties to the Pòrt de Caldes springs; there is no vehicle access beyond the Artiga.
notes: Cold, late ground where rovellons flush from mid-October, and the long walk-in keeps pressure minimal.

name: Lac de Mar
access: From Salardú take the Valarties road and pull off at the Lac de Mar bridge; continue on foot up the east-bank track.
notes: Ordinary pine with patchy moss that produces in bursts after the first autumn rains, with local families out at weekends.

name: Pinedes de Gessa
access: From Salardú take the short road to Gessa; park at the upper end of the village and climb the track onto the west slopes.
notes: A mossy west-facing belt that holds the dew and fruits steadily from late September in wet years.

name: Bassa d'Oles
access: From Salardú take the road through Gessa and Bagergue up to the Bassa d'Oles; park at the pond lay-by.
notes: Classic late ground — often the last snow-free rovelló beds of the valley in early November.

name: Solana de Bossòst
access: From Bossòst take the lane behind the church that zigzags onto the south slope; park where the tarmac ends at the cistern.
notes: A warm, early slope that gives the first rovellons of the season but bakes dry within days without rain.

name: Obaga de Bossòst
access: From Bossòst take the N-230 north towards Les and the border; pull onto the forest track on the left, park at the hairpin gate and climb on foot.
notes: Shady and damp, carrying a second flush later in November once the solana has dried out.

name: Costes de Malpàs
access: From El Pont de Suert take the road up to Malpàs; park at the edge of the village and follow the track onto the north-west slopes.
notes: Mid-season ground on stony soil that needs a good September soak before it produces.

name: Solà de Corroncui
access: From El Pont de Suert take the winding road to Corroncui; park at the village and take the track along the sun-facing ridge.
notes: Light picking pressure but thin moss, so it is only productive in consistently wet autumns.

name: Pineda de Taüll
access: From Barruera take the road up to Taüll; park below the Romanesque tower and climb the tracks along the ski-slope edges.
notes: A busy tourist valley — go on weekdays, as the high beds here keep fruiting into November.

name: Feixancs de Durro
access: From Barruera take the road to Durro; park at the top of the village and follow the terrace path onto the south-west face.
notes: A quiet, mossy face where the old terraces keep the humidity, making it a reliable late-October producer.

name: Obaga d'Erill la Vall
access: From Barruera take the road to Erill la Vall; park by the church and take the track onto the shady side above the campsite.
notes: Damp and steady — it arrives about a week before the higher beds and holds on with the autumn mists.

name: Solà d'Escaló
access: From la Guingueta take the road to Escaló; park at the village gate and climb the track onto the sunny slope above the gorge.
notes: An early, fast-drying slope that is worth only the first two weeks after the September rains.

name: Vall d'Unarre
access: From Escaló take the rough lane up the val d'Unarre; park at the first gate and continue on foot along the east flank.
notes: A quiet, humid corner with little traffic and mossy beds that produce through October.

name: Solana de Llavorsí
access: From Llavorsí cross the bridge towards the Sort road and take the first forest track on the left; park at the bend and climb the sunny side.
notes: Handy to town so it gets picked over early — best in the first days after an autumn storm.

name: Obaga de Llavorsí
access: From Llavorsí take the lane towards the chapel above the village; park at the track gate and continue along the shady flank.
notes: Thick, mossy pine that keeps its moisture — a solid mid-October sector with modest pressure.

name: Solà de Tírvia
access: From Tírvia take the road up to the mirador above the village; park at the viewpoint and drop onto the sunny benches.
notes: An easy family slope near the village that takes heavy weekend pressure once the season opens.

name: Obaga d'Estaron
access: From Tírvia take the lane towards Estaron; park at the last house and follow the track onto the north-east face.
notes: Cool and damp, often carrying the last rovellons of the lower Pallars into late November.

name: Costes de Sant Salvador de Toló
access: From Gavet take the road up to Sant Salvador de Toló; park at the village and follow the track onto the north-west slopes.
notes: Ordinary pine on stony ground that fruits in bursts, so time a visit after a wet week.

name: Solà de Gavet
access: From Gavet take the track behind the village church onto the sunny ridge; park where the track narrows at the pines.
notes: Thin, open cover that dries quickly — an early-season option while the higher zones are still parched.

name: Obaga de Sant Gervàs
access: From Tremp take the road towards Puigcercós and continue to the north flank of the serra; park at the water tank and enter the woods.
notes: Close to Tremp, so it bears the town's weekend pickers — be there at first light in October.

name: Solà de Puigcercós
access: From Tremp take the road to Puigcercós; park at the edge of the abandoned quarter and take the track along the sunny side of the ridge.
notes: A warm slope that opens the season early but gives out unless the rains keep coming.

name: Solà de Guàrdia de Mur
access: From the C-147 take the road up to Guàrdia de Mur; park below the castle and follow the track onto the south-west slopes.
notes: Scattered beds under thin cover that reward a slow, patient circuit in late October.

name: Obaga de Santa Llúcia
access: From Guàrdia de Mur continue on the lane to Santa Llúcia de Mur; park at the hamlet and climb the shady track behind the church.
notes: A north face that stays green late — one of the last producing corners of the Conca in November.

name: Costes de Santa Maria de Meià
access: From Vilanova de Meià take the road towards Santa Maria de Meià; park at the old canonical house and climb onto the south-east slopes.
notes: Karstic, fast-draining ground that flushes briefly but heavily after the autumn storms.

name: Serrat de la Corona
access: From Vilanova de Meià take the track up the north side of the massif towards the Corona; park at the col gate and work the shady side.
notes: Deep moss and very little traffic — the massif's most reliable late-October beds.

name: Costes de Tragó
access: From Os de Balaguer take the road to Tragó de Segre; park at the village and follow the channel-side path onto the south-east slopes.
notes: Low and warm, so the first rovellons of the Noguera appear here, but the picking window is short.

name: Feixes del Montsec
access: From Os de Balaguer take the track that climbs behind the village towards the Montsec foot; park at the first bench of terraces.
notes: Town-adjacent ground under steady local pressure — pick it in the first days after rain.

name: Obaga d'Anserall
access: From Anserall take the track up the left bank of the Valira towards Arcavell; park at the bend below the old bridge and follow the path into the north-facing pines.
notes: Cool north slopes that hold moisture late into October, with moderate weekend pressure from La Seu pickers.

name: Pines above Ars
access: From Ars climb the fire track east of the village; park at the water tank and continue on foot through the pine stands.
notes: Drier east-facing pinewood that fruits best after autumn storms, and sees little pressure beyond local families.

name: Obaga d'Alàs
access: From Alàs take the forest track behind the church towards the Cerc side; park where the track forks above the fields and walk into the obaga.
notes: Ordinary Scots pine on the obaga that produces steadily in wet Octobers with very light picking pressure.

name: Serres east slopes
access: From Serres follow the lane east past the last barns; park at the track gate and walk the sunny edge of the pinewood.
notes: East-facing ordinary pine that needs a good rain to fruit but is barely picked after the early season.

name: Cadí north faces of Arsèguel
access: From Arsèguel follow the Cadí trail westwards; park at the fountain above the village and climb into the north-face black pine belt.
notes: High mossy black pine that holds dew well and fruits after the first cold nights, with almost no pressure given the long climb.

name: Obaga d'Arsèguel
access: From the road above Arsèguel take the track into the obaga north-east of the village; park at the first hairpin and continue on foot.
notes: Shadier and earlier than the high canals, good in late September but small in dry years.

name: Vall Major north slopes
access: From the road towards Castellbò park at the mirador bend above the valley; take the footpath into the pines on the north side.
notes: Ordinary Scots pine close to La Seu so it gets picked early on October weekends.

name: Segre left-bank pines
access: From the road to Montferrer park at the quarry bend; walk up the south-east facing track through open pine.
notes: Warm open pine that fruits early and dries out fast, best checked right after the first September rains.

name: Rigolisa north belt
access: From Puigcerdà take the road towards Rigolisa; park at the chapel and follow the track north-east into the pine belt.
notes: Popular ribbon of mossy Scots pine minutes from Puigcerdà, heavily picked on weekends so go at dawn.

name: Serra east of Rigolisa
access: From Rigolisa continue on the farm track towards the border fence; park at the last barn and cut east into the pines.
notes: Slightly drier than the north side but with steady September flushes and steady pressure from town.

name: Serra d'Avellanida east
access: From the N-260 between Puigcerdà and Bolvir take the forest track onto the serra; park at the water deposit and walk east along the crest.
notes: Well-trodden serra pine with reliable moss, among the first Cerdanya spots to fruit and correspondingly picked.

name: Serra d'Avellanida west
access: From Puigcerdà take the road towards Bolvir and turn off at the golf course; park at the track gate and head west up the serra.
notes: Quieter west end of the serra with thinner soils, decent after rain but patchy in dry autumns.

name: Pla de Martiva north
access: From Bolvir follow the signs for Pla de Martiva on the dirt track; park at the picnic clearing and explore the pines north of the track.
notes: Flat accessible woods that fruit early and are swept by local families within days of a good rain.

name: Pla de Martiva south edge
access: From Bolvir take the Martiva track and continue past the picnic area; park at the second bend where the pines open to the south.
notes: Sunnier edge that fruits in flushes after storms and sees slightly less pressure than the north side.

name: Segre terraces at Prats
access: From Prats i Sansor take the lane down towards the Segre; park at the irrigation channel bridge and climb the south-facing pine slope.
notes: Low warm Scots pine that fruits early and lightly, mostly visited by villagers from Prats and Sansor.

name: Obaga above Prats i Sansor
access: From the N-260 at Prats take the track up the valley side; park at the sheepfold and continue on foot into the north-west facing pines.
notes: Moister obaga with steady late-October tail production when the lower slopes have dried.

name: Cadí faces above Estana
access: From Estana follow the Cadí park trail westwards; park at the barrier above the village and climb into the north-face black pine belt.
notes: Superb mossy black pine that holds moisture into November, with light pressure thanks to the stiff climb.

name: Obaga east of Estana
access: From Estana take the track behind the church to the north-east; park where it becomes a path and descend into the shaded black pine.
notes: Earlier and lower than the crest canals, productive right after the first autumn cold snaps.

name: North-west crest above Estana
access: From the Estana track continue past the last gate to the north-west; leave the car at the turning circle and walk the path along the crest.
notes: High exposed sector with thin but quality moss patches, best in wet years and barely visited.

name: Pla de Pardines
access: From Pardines take the road towards Llanars and turn onto the plateau track; park at the telecommunications mast and work the pine flats.
notes: Classic Ripollès plateau pine that fruits generously after September storms and draws weekend pickers from the valley.

name: Serrat south of Pardines
access: From Pardines follow the forest track south past the hay barns; park at the bend and enter the east-facing pines.
notes: Slightly quieter east slope with good moss cover, fruiting a few days after the plateaus.

name: Slope above Llanars
access: From Llanars follow the track behind the sports field up the north-east slope; park at the water tank and continue on foot.
notes: Mossy mixed pine just above the village, popular with Ripollès pickers and often swept by mid-morning.

name: Costes de Llanars
access: From the road between Llanars and Vilallonga park at the hairpin; take the path up the north-facing slope into denser pine.
notes: Darker north slope that holds moisture longest and keeps producing into late October.

name: Solana de Llanars
access: From the main valley road at the Llanars exit take the paved lane up the sunny side; park at the last farmhouse and walk the track through open pine.
notes: Warm open pine that fruits in fast flushes right after rain but shuts down quickly in dry spells.

name: Vall de Ter north slopes
access: From Vilallonga de Ter take the track up the right-hand side of the valley; park at the bridge over the torrent and climb into the north-west pines.
notes: Good mossy belt above the Ter with moderate pressure from Camprodon pickers.

name: Pines above Abella
access: From Vilallonga continue to Abella; park at the church and follow the path south-east through the pine.
notes: Lower drier slope around Abella that produces early and lightly before the high sectors start.

name: Puigsacalm foothills
access: From Les Planes d'Hostoles take the road towards Sant Feliu de Pallerols; park at the first hairpin after the village and take the footpath north-west into the Scots pine.
notes: Humid Garrotxa foothill pine that fruits well after wet late summers with only local pressure.

name: Solana de les Planes
access: From Les Planes follow the track up the sunny side above the village; park at the reservoir track gate and walk up through open pine.
notes: Easy-access southern slope that fruits in pulses after storms and sees weekend families from Olot.

name: Pines of Hostalnou
access: From Hostalnou de Bianya take the side track towards Sant Salvador de Bianya; park at the church and work the pine slopes east.
notes: Quiet mossy pine around the old priory with steady production and very light picking pressure.

name: Capsacosta pass
access: From Hostalnou continue towards Sant Salvador de Bianya and park where the track forks; follow the old path up to the Capsacosta pass and into the north-facing pine.
notes: High damp pass pine with quality moss, slow to fruit but lasting into November and barely picked.

name: Sant Pere Despuig slopes
access: From Sant Pere Despuig take the lane east past the last houses; park at the track gate and walk the south-east facing pine.
notes: Ordinary pine on a quiet hamlet slope, patchy in dry years but untouched by outside pickers.

name: Obaga de Beuda
access: From Beuda take the lane north past the church; park at the barns below the village and follow the path into the north-west pines.
notes: Small mossy pockets on the obaga that fruit after autumn storms, with almost no pressure.

name: Solana de Beuda
access: From the road between Beuda and Palera park at the bend; take the track up the sunny slope through open pine.
notes: Early warm slope that gives a first flush in September and then depends on repeat rains.

name: Obaga del Cadí de Gréixer
access: From Guardiola de Berguedà take the B-402 towards Saldes and turn off at Gréixer; park at the track gate below the Cadí tunnel south portal.
notes: High, cold and late — the black pine belt here holds moisture well into November but fruits only after steady autumn rain.

name: Costa del Túnel
access: From Guardiola de Berguedà take the B-402 to the Gréixer turnoff and follow the forest track up beside the tunnel access road; park at the bend by the water tank.
notes: Shaded and reliably damp, though the easy track means Barcelonan pickers work it hard on October weekends.

name: Serrat de Gréixer
access: From Gréixer village take the signed track towards the Serrat shepherds' huts; park at the closed barrier past the last barn.
notes: A mix of Scots and black pine with good moss cover that produces after the first cold nights, usually a week behind the valleys.

name: Obaga de Catllaràs
access: From Vilada take the BV-4031 towards La Pobla de Lillet and then the Catllaràs track on the right; park at the old fountain bend.
notes: The classic Catllaràs obaga holds humidity long after rain but is a fixture on weekend Berga circuits — go at first light.

name: Serrat de Vilada
access: From Vilada take the minor road towards Sant Julià de Cerdanyola and pull onto the dirt track at the crest; park in the grassy lay-by by the pylon.
notes: Drier and earlier than the obaga above, often the first belt to fruit near Vilada but thins out fast in dry Octobers.

name: Obaga Major
access: From La Quar take the track that climbs behind the church towards the upper pastures; park at the gate where the tarmac ends.
notes: Deep mossy Scots pine that keeps moisture well, though the climb keeps casual pickers away and pressure stays moderate.

name: Boscos de Sant Maurici
access: From La Quar take the local road towards Sant Maurici and continue on the farm track; park at the turning circle by the chapel track.
notes: Lower and sunnier, so it fruits early in the season and is largely finished once the obagues higher up start producing.

name: Mirador de Castellar del Riu
access: From Castellar del Riu take the signed road to the famous viewpoint; park at the mirador car park and take either path down.
notes: Popular for the views as much as the mushrooms, so the ring within a kilometre of the car park is picked clean by mid-morning.

name: Serra de Castellar del Riu
access: From Castellar del Riu take the forest track heading northeast along the serra crest; park at the barrier past the last house and continue on foot.
notes: A rich mossy transition belt between Scots and black pine that holds late-season moisture, rewarding the long walk with sizeable groups.

name: Serra de l'Espunyola
access: From L'Espunyola take the road towards Casserres and turn onto the serra track at the crest; park at the wide bend by the water deposit.
notes: Quiet, well-mossified Scots pine on the pre-Pyrenean edge that produces steadily in wet autumns with little picking pressure.

name: Obaga del Riu d'Espunyola
access: From L'Espunyola take the track down towards the stream and follow the obaga upstream; park at the concrete ford by the old mill.
notes: A shaded streamside belt that keeps dew late into the morning, dependable in mediocre years when the high country stays dry.

name: Vora del Llobregat
access: From Puig-reig take the C-16 frontage road towards Gironella and turn off at the riverside track; park at the clearing under the pines by the old weir.
notes: Low riverside pine that fruits early and heavily after the first September rains but is a weekend family favourite from the town.

name: Serra de Galliners
access: From Puig-reig take the BV-4235 towards Montmajor and pull onto the forest track at the Galliners sign; park at the junction by the transformer hut.
notes: A modest but little-visited belt above the Llobregat that keeps moisture on its north face and surprises in consistently rainy autumns.

name: Riu Negre
access: From Olius take the lane down to the Riu Negre and follow the left-bank track; park at the ford below the old bridge.
notes: Sheltered valley pine near Solsona that fruits dependably in mid-season, though Sunday walkers from the town thin it out.

name: Serrat d'Olius
access: From Olius take the track climbing towards the serra north of the village; park at the gate where the track narrows to a path.
notes: Mossy obaga heights that hold dew and produce a solid second flush in late October with moderate competition from locals.

name: Mirador de Castelltallat
access: From Lladurs take the signed road to the Mirador de Castelltallat; park at the viewpoint car park and work the open pine below.
notes: Sunny, open pine near the famous telecoms church, early to fruit and heavily worked on holiday weekends by Solsona pickers.

name: Obaga de Castelltallat
access: From Lladurs take the track that follows the northern flank of the Castelltallat range; park at the closed forest gate past the last mas.
notes: The shady back of Castelltallat keeps moisture far longer than the mirador side and yields good groups to those willing to walk.

name: Coma de Lladurs
access: From Lladurs village take the northeast track into the coma; park at the bend by the small spring enclosure.
notes: A tucked-away hollow of Scots pine with rich soil that local families keep quiet, producing best after two consecutive wet weeks.

name: Pinedes de Castelladral
access: From Súria take the BV-3001 towards Castelladral and turn onto the forest track at the hillside bend; park at the clearing by the shrine.
notes: The best-known pine slope above Súria, early and productive after September storms but worked over by local families at weekends.

name: Serrat del Roi
access: From Súria take the road towards Callús and pull onto the track at the Roi signpost; park at the wide verge by the olive terrace.
notes: A low, mixed belt where Scots pine mingles with Aleppo pine — fast to fruit after rain but quick to dry out in between.

name: Bosc del Castell de Rajadell
access: From Rajadell take the lane up to the castle ruin; park at the small esplanade below the walls and take any of the west paths.
notes: A quiet, easily reached slope with modest but reliable production, mostly gathered by a handful of Manresa foragers.

name: Serra de Rajadell
access: From Rajadell take the BV-3002 towards Fonollosa and turn onto the serra track; park at the flat bend by the water tank.
notes: Denser north-face pine that keeps the morning dew and gives a late-October flush when the lower Bages is already finished.

name: Serrat de Fonollosa
access: From Fonollosa take the track northeast along the serrat; park at the gate past the last masia and continue on foot.
notes: Little-visited Bages pine with patchy but worthwhile groups in wet years, mostly untouched outside the immediate village.

name: Obaga de Fonollosa
access: From Fonollosa take the lane down towards the stream and follow the obaga track upstream; park at the old cement ford.
notes: A shady hollow holding humidity late in the season, rewarding the rough track with a respectable second flush.

name: Riu Calders
access: From Calders take the lane towards the river below the village; park at the picnic area by the old bridge.
notes: Riverside pine that fruits early after the first rains, a convenient evening spot for Moianès locals and thus quickly picked.

name: Costa de Calders
access: From Calders take the track climbing north out of the valley; park at the barrier at the top of the first switchbacks.
notes: Mossy upper slopes with genuine rovelló habitat that stays productive into November with barely any weekend pressure.

name: Vora del Monestir
access: From L'Estany take the road past the monastery of Santa Maria de l'Estany; park in the small lot by the picnic tables.
notes: Gentle, accessible pine around the monastery that fruits early and is a traditional family outing, so mornings matter.

name: Serra de l'Estany
access: From L'Estany take the track up onto the serra behind the village; park at the closed gate by the communication mast.
notes: A quiet Moianès height with dense mossy pine that few people walk, producing good groups through late October.

name: Pla d'Olost
access: From Olost take the BV-4601 towards Prats de Lluçanès and turn onto the plateau track; park on the verge by the first pine stand.
notes: Typical open Lluçanès plateau pine that gives light early crops and dries fast, best checked right after September rain.

name: Obaga d'Olost
access: From Olost take the lane north towards Sant Agustí de Lluçanès and pull onto the obaga track; park at the farm gate at the wood's edge.
notes: One of the better-kept Lluçanès secrets — a north-facing belt that holds moisture and yields steady groups with minimal pressure.

name: Voltants de Sant Esteve
access: From Perafita take the short road up to the church of Sant Esteve; park in the esplanade by the cemetery and follow any path down.
notes: Easy family pine around the landmark church that produces modest early crops and is picked over by village children first.

name: Serra de Perafita
access: From Perafita take the track climbing onto the serra towards the Girona border; park at the barrier where the track degenerates to a path.
notes: High, quiet Lluçanès pine with thick moss that keeps producing into November, well worth the walk from the barrier.

name: Cingles de Sora
access: From Sora take the track along the top of the Ter gorge cliffs; park at the viewpoint clearing and descend the west-facing paths.
notes: Cliff-top pine with sea-of-fog moisture from the gorge, giving strong mid-season flushes but a fair few pickers from Osona.

name: Obaga del Ter
access: From Sora take the footpath down towards the Ter and follow the shady bank downstream; there is no parking closer than the village fountain.
notes: The damp heart of the gorge — long to reach but the mossy Scots pine here holds the best and least-picked rovellons of the sector.

name: Costa de Sora
access: From Sora take the uphill track towards the eastern pastures; park at the bend by the stone shelter and work the slope below.
notes: A sunny upper belt that fruits in bursts after cold-front rain, quieter than the cingles and good as an early-season backup.

name: Parc del Castell de Montesquiu
access: From Montesquiu take the park road to the castle; park in the main car park and take any of the waymarked park paths.
notes: The castle park's accessible pine fills with weekenders from Vic and Barcelona, so only the far loops hold unpicked groups.

name: Obaga de Montesquiu
access: From Montesquiu take the BV-4226 towards Sora and turn onto the north-side forest track; park at the gate by the stream crossing.
notes: The shaded slope above the Ter holds dew all morning and keeps producing after the park side is stripped, with far fewer people.

name: Sant Segimon
access: From Arbúcies take the Sant Segimon road north past Can Pallot and continue to the end of the forest track; park at the clearing below the shrine.
notes: Mossy north-face beds that hold their dew well into the morning, though the easy track means crowds sweep them early on autumn Sundays.

name: Serrat de Can Pla
access: From Arbúcies take the C-63 toward Sant Hilari and turn onto the Can Pla track after the last houses; park at the gate by the pasture.
notes: East-facing slopes that dry out fast after rain, so come within two or three days of a good October soaking.

name: Sant Marçal
access: From Arbúcies follow the Sant Marçal road up through the upper belt to the pass; park at the small lot outside the chapel gates.
notes: High mossy belt that only opens in November when the lower woods are finished, and the long climb keeps weekend pressure moderate.

name: Serrat de la Guàrdia
access: From Vidreres take the C-35 toward Maçanet and turn off onto the forest track by the water tank; park at the track gate.
notes: Ordinary mixed pine that needs a full wet week to produce, and quiet midweek picking on the Vilobí side leaves some untouched patches.

name: Turó de les Closes
access: From Vidreres take the road toward Llagostera and park at the wide bend by the Mas Ros track.
notes: Dry south-facing Aleppo pine that only fruits after heavy autumn storms, so it is a quick-stop spot rather than a guarantee.

name: Serrat de Puitjà
access: From Sant Gregori take the Bescanó road and turn onto the Puitjà track at the quarry bend; park at the flat below the chapel.
notes: A north-facing bank above the Ter basin that keeps some humidity, but Girona weekenders work it hard.

name: Costa de la Llémena
access: From Sant Gregori follow the Llémena valley road toward Sant Aniol and take the Can Barra track uphill; park at the spring clearing.
notes: Productive soils at the valley mouth where the first late-September rains bring early flushes before the Gavarres get going.

name: Puig d'Arques
access: From Cassà take the Santa Pellaia road and continue on the Gavarres track past Mas Alió; park at the gate below the northern summit slopes.
notes: The classic Gavarres north face, mossy and reliable after October rains, but expect company at dawn.

name: Sant Miquel de Casseres
access: From Cassà take the Can Cassò road toward the northwest and follow the signs to Sant Miquel; park beside the small church.
notes: Sheltered hollows around the chapel hold moisture well into November and spread pickers across many small canals.

name: Serrat de les Alzines
access: From Cassà take the C-65 toward Llambilles and turn off at the telecoms mast; park at the Caseta track gate.
notes: Transitional pine that yields only in short windows after steady rain, and mostly locals so midweek it is quiet.

name: Serrat d'Usall
access: From Banyoles take the GI-513 toward Usall and park at the bend where the tarmac becomes a forest track.
notes: A west-facing serrat that catches the afternoon sun, giving good early-season flushes when late September is wet.

name: Costa de Mata
access: From Usall take the rural lane toward the Mata farmhouses; park at the track gate by the sheepfold.
notes: Low rolling pine over clay that goes quickly in dry years and is often better in the second flush of November.

name: Serrat del Faig
access: From Cornellà del Terri take the road toward Sant Miquel de Campmajor and park at the forest track on the left below the crest.
notes: A north slope that keeps the valley damp, and a locals' wood that produces steadily after the October storms.

name: Costa de les Corts
access: From Cornellà del Terri take the lane toward Riudellots and park at the track bend by the water deposit.
notes: Dry, easy-access pine that suits a family morning but stays thin unless the autumn has been wet.

name: Serrat de Solius
access: From Santa Cristina d'Aro take the road up to Solius past the monastery; park at the fountain above the last houses.
notes: A shady north-facing bank inside the Gavarres that fruits well after sea-fog weeks and is a favourite of Aro valley pickers.

name: Serrat de Bell-lloc
access: From Santa Cristina d'Aro take the Bell-lloc lane west out of town; park at the track gate by the water tank.
notes: A south-facing crest above the coast that dries fast, so time it right after rain or miss it.

name: Costes de Romanyà
access: From Calonge take the Vall de Calonge road north and turn off at the Romanyà signs; park at the Gavarres track gate past the hamlet.
notes: Mossy northwest slopes above the valley that hold the dew, but Romanyà's fame brings heavy weekend pressure.

name: Serrat de Can Llobet
access: From Calonge follow the Vall de Calonge road north and park where the asphalt ends at the last working farmhouse.
notes: An east-facing slope that warms early and is one of the first south-side Gavarres spots to fruit each season.

name: Costes de Requesens
access: From Espolla take the Requesens track south into the Albera and park at the first saddle below the transmission line.
notes: Cool north slopes of the Albera that keep the moisture of the Tramuntana rains, and far enough from any town that pressure stays minimal.

name: Serrat de Vilartolí
access: From Espolla take the lane toward Vilartolí and continue on the forest track; park at the bend above the last farmhouse.
notes: South-facing Albera slopes that bake dry under the north wind and are best in the first mild, humid week of November.

name: Serrat del Bosc
access: From Capmany take the GI-602 toward Sant Climent and turn onto the forest track at the last masia; park at the first gate.
notes: Gently shelving pine over granite sand that drains fast and needs a truly wet autumn, then fruits suddenly.

name: Serrat de la Pineda
access: From Capmany take the lane west toward Biure and park at the track gate by the vineyard shed.
notes: Warm west-facing pine among the vineyards and a reliable early-season spot for locals before the high woods open.

name: Turó del Corredor
access: From Dosrius take the road up to the Corredor sanctuary; park in the small lot by the restaurant at the pass.
notes: The best-known rovelló wood in the Maresme, mossy and productive, but you must be on the path by dawn on autumn Sundays.

name: Serra de Canyamars
access: From Dosrius take the road to Canyamars and turn up the serra track past the fire cistern; park where the track forks.
notes: The east flank catches the morning damp off the sea, so it is heavily worked at weekends and best on weekdays.

name: Serrat de Can Boquet
access: From Dosrius take the Canyamars road and turn left onto the Can Boquet track; park at the bend by the water tank.
notes: A warm south face that closes early in dry years, worth only on the first cool, wet week of October.

name: Serrat de Mata
access: From Arenys de Munt take the lane up past El Rieral and continue on the forest track toward Mata; park at the clearing by the old spring.
notes: North-facing woods that trap the sea moisture and a Barcelona train-and-boot classic, so expect many baskets on Sundays.

name: Serrat de la Creu
access: From Arenys de Munt take the road down toward Arenys de Mar and turn onto the forest track at the last masia; park at the bend by the pines.
notes: Lower, warmer pine that fruits in bursts after sea storms and is worth checking on damp, cloudy afternoons.

name: Serrat de les Salzes
access: From Argentona take the Òrrius road and turn up the Salzes track; park at the quarry bend.
notes: Sheltered northeast hollows that keep the last of the dew, though Mataró pickers sweep them early on weekends.

name: Serrat del Rost
access: From Argentona take the road toward Dosrius and park at the bend where the asphalt ends below the serra.
notes: East-facing open pine on shallow soil that is only worth it after steady autumn rain, but then it surprises.

name: Puig de la Creu
access: From El Catllar take the road towards Vespella and turn off on the gravel track at the last vineyards; park at the bend where the pines take over.
notes: Warm mixed pine that fruits early after the first autumn storms, though Tarragona weekenders pick it hard.

name: Riba del Gaià
access: From El Catllar take the road to la Riera de Gaià and turn north on the paved farm lane at the bridge over the Gaià; park beside the old mill.
notes: Low Aleppo along the river needs a wet October to produce, but sea-fog mornings keep it going longer than expected.

name: Serra de la Creu
access: From El Catllar take the road towards Vespella and fork left onto the forest track before the last mas; park at the water tank on the crest.
notes: The shadier north slope keeps its moss damp, so it carries on producing after the valley pines have dried out.

name: Serra de Vespella
access: From Vespella de Gaià take the track behind the church up onto the serra; park at the turning circle by the antennas.
notes: One of the better Gaià-side pine belts; go on weekday mornings because Tarragona families sweep it in season.

name: Costes de la Quadra
access: From Vespella de Gaià take the paved lane east towards la Nou de Gaià and continue on the dirt track past the ruins of la Quadra; park at the bend below the pines.
notes: West-facing Aleppo that only fruits well after repeated autumn rains and then finishes within days.

name: Serra del Tolós
access: From El Pla de Santa Maria take the road towards Aiguamúrcia and turn off at Selmà onto the forest track; park where the track bends under the north-facing pines.
notes: Quiet foothill Scots pine that locals keep quiet about; the first hard frosts end the season abruptly.

name: Pinedes de Cabra
