access: From El Pla de Santa Maria take the road towards Cabra del Camp and follow the gravel track past the reservoir; park at the firebreak gate.
notes: Ordinary pine but with very few pickers, so mornings after drizzle can be surprisingly productive.

name: Cim de la Serra de Miramar
access: From El Miramar take the track past the church of Sant Martí up onto the serra; park at the col where the GR crosses the crest.
notes: High, quiet Scots pine that holds dew late into the morning, with a season that runs later than the coast.

name: Obagues de Miramar
access: From El Miramar take the lane towards the scattered masies and continue on the forest track into the gully; park at the spring below the pines.
notes: Shady gully pines on deep soil — among the last stands with rovellons when autumn stays dry.

name: Serra del Gaià
access: From Sant Martí Sarroca take the road towards Pontons and turn right onto the track above the vineyards; park at the clearing at the top of the bend.
notes: A good upper-Gaià pine belt that keeps fruiting through November in wet years.

name: La Múnia
access: From Sant Martí Sarroca take the road towards la Múnia and follow the dirt track beyond the last mas; park at the tank on the saddle.
notes: Quiet, mossy Scots pine that rewards early walks two or three days after rain.

name: Boscos del Castell de Mediona
access: From Mediona take the track signposted to the castle; park at the fold below the castle walls.
notes: Deep-soil pine under the castle that holds moisture well into December.

name: Capçaleres del Foix
access: From Mediona follow the lane upstream along the Foix; park at the ford where the track narrows.
notes: Dense pine along the headwaters — the best local stands after a wet October and still uncrowded.

name: Sant Joan de Mediona
access: From Mediona take the road towards Sant Joan de Mediona and continue on the track past the church; park at the old corrals at the edge of the pine.
notes: West-facing but tall pine; productive in stormy autumns and you will rarely meet another picker.

name: Serra de Banyeres
access: From Banyeres del Penedès take the track up behind the sports field onto the serra; park at the water depot on the crest.
notes: Small-town pine that bursts a week after the first storms and is picked out by mid-morning on Sundays.

name: Coma de l'Àliga
access: From Banyeres del Penedès take the paved farm road east among the vineyards and continue on the dirt track; park at the bend below the pine hill.
notes: Dry, open Aleppo on limestone that is only worth checking late in a rainy season, when the shaded hollows surprise.

name: Serra de Santa Oliva
access: From Santa Oliva take the road towards Castellet and turn onto the forest track at the first rise; park at the pull-in by the pines.
notes: Coastal-range Aleppo that wakes up after autumn storms; modest hauls but easy walking.

name: Bosc de Dalt
access: From Santa Oliva take the track north-east past the masies; park at the cistern where the pine closes over.
notes: A touch more Scots on the shady side means it fruits a little later and better than the pure Aleppo below.

name: Pla de Palau
access: From Olivella take the road towards Sitges and turn off at the Pla de Palau track; park at the fire tank by the track junction.
notes: Dry Garraf Aleppo that only produces after a stormy autumn, when the shaded north hollows fill quickly.

name: Turó de la Creu
access: From Olivella take the lane behind the cemetery north-east and continue on foot past the barrier; park at the barrier clearing.
notes: Popular with Sitges foragers — anything showing is picked within hours, so go at first light after rain.

name: Serra d'Ordal nord
access: From Begues take the road towards Sant Llorenç d'Ordal and turn off on the forest track after the second rise; park at the clearing by the pylon.
notes: The best-drained north slopes around Begues hold a late November crop, but expect company from the Baix Llobregat.

name: Pinedes de la Riera
access: From Begues follow the lane up the riera past the last houses; park at the picnic clearing where the track forks.
notes: Shadier and slightly damper than the crest, so it fruits after smaller rains than the rest of the range.

name: Serra de l'Ataix
access: From Torrelles de Llobregat take the road towards Sant Climent and turn onto the track at the foot of the serra; park at the bend by the vineyard.
notes: Metropolitan pine that gets swept early — after a stormy night you have perhaps two good mornings.

name: Pinedes de Ponent
access: From Torrelles de Llobregat take the road towards Santa Coloma and pull onto the farm track after the second bend; park at the water tank.
notes: Warm west-facing Aleppo that needs a wet week to fruit; easy access makes it a family favourite in October.

name: Serralada de Cerilles
access: From Santa Coloma de Cervelló take the road towards Cervelló and turn off at the Cerilles track; park at the gate on the crest.
notes: The closest north-facing pine to Sant Boi and Sant Just, picked within minutes of sunrise on rainy weekends.

name: Obagues del Torrent
access: From Santa Coloma de Cervelló take the lane up towards Collserola behind the cemetery and continue on the forest track; park at the saddle by the pylon.
notes: A quiet gully of tall Aleppo that keeps humidity and produces steadily, if modestly, in wet autumns.

name: Vallvidrera
access: From Barcelona take the Vallvidrera road to the village and follow the track from the Font de la Budellera into the north woods; park at the font.
notes: Heavily picked metropolitan woods — rovellons appear after storms but rarely survive the first weekend morning.

name: Can Caralleu
access: From Barcelona take the Ronda de Dalt to the Can Caralleu exit and park at the sports centre; take the trail behind the complex uphill.
notes: Every patch near the centre is picked within hours of rain, so arrive before dawn or not at all.

name: Sant Medir
access: From Barcelona take the road up from Esplugues to the Sant Medir shrine; park at the clearing by the shrine.
notes: Families and school groups strip these slopes, though the shady draws still yield small late flushes.

name: Valldoreix
access: From Valldoreix take the paved lane up to the water tank below the turó and park there; follow the path north into the woods.
notes: A Valès pine belt within walking distance of the station, so expect dozens of pickers on any Sunday in season.

name: Can Mira-sol
access: From Sant Cugat take the road past Can Mira-sol and continue on the forest track after the barrier; park at the barrier.
notes: East-facing and quick to dry, so time it right after rain amid constant dog-walker traffic.

name: Serra de Galliners
area: Sant Quirze del Vallès · Serra de Galliners
access: From Sant Quirze del Vallès take the road towards Terrassa and turn off at the Galliners track; park at the clearing on the crest.
notes: A low, warm crest that fruits early and briefly, and is known flush by flush to local pickers.

name: Galliners de Ponent
area: Sant Quirze del Vallès · Serra de Galliners
access: From Sant Quirze del Vallès take the lane west past the last houses and continue on the dirt track to the end of the serra; park at the cistern.
notes: A few Scots pines on the shadier end keep it going a week longer than the crest.

name: Sant Elies de Vilamajor
access: From Sant Pere de Vilamajor take the road up to Sant Elies and park at the church; follow the track north into the pines.
notes: Classic mossy Montseny north-facing Scots pine — dependable after autumn rains and busier every year.

name: Obagues de Vilamajor
access: From Sant Pere de Vilamajor take the track north-east past the last masies; park at the spring where the pine begins.
notes: A lower belt mixed with Aleppo that starts earlier than Sant Elies; go on weekdays to beat the Granollers crowd.

name: Sant Miquel del Fai
access: From Bigues take the road towards Sant Miquel del Fai and park at the bend below the sanctuary; follow the old path up the north slope above the gorge.
notes: Dense, damp pine above the gorge — good rovelló ground, but the Fai crowds demand an early start.

name: Serrat de Riells
access: From Riells del Fai take the lane up past the church and continue on the forest track onto the serrat; park at the track end.
notes: A quiet serrat of mixed pine that holds dew and is a reliable fallback when the Fai paths are picked clean.

name: Tossal Gros
access: From Ascó take the track behind the sports centre towards the tossals and follow the fire road up; park at the clearing below the transmitter mast.
notes: A narrow Aleppo belt that wakes with the first October storms and is worked quickly by locals — go within days of good rain.

name: Serra de Lloreta
access: From Ascó cross the Ebre on the C-12 heading south and take the vineyard track at the first bend; park at the shed at the foot of the serra.
notes: Denser east-facing pinewood that keeps damp into late October; quiet on weekdays but busy with hunters at weekends.

name: Obagues de Cavalls
access: From Tivissa take the road toward la Torre de l'Espanyol, park at the track junction below the crest and climb the north-facing firebreaks.
notes: Mixed pine on shaded Cavalls slopes that fruits steadily after September rain; most pressure comes at weekends.

name: Llevant de Cavalls
access: From Tivissa take the road toward Darmós and turn onto the olive-grove track at the second bend; park at the pond by the ruined mas.
notes: Open eastern slope that needs a proper storm to get going; late October and November give the best windows.

name: Serra de Llaberia sud
access: From Tivissa take the road toward Pradell de la Teixeta and park where the track to the antennas leaves the pass; follow the path into the pines.
notes: Cool dense pinewood that holds moisture from the first storms; expect a long walk and almost no other pickers midweek.

name: Serra de la Fatalla
access: From El Perelló take the C-44 towards l'Ametlla de Mar for 4 km, then the forest track signed to the serra; park at the clearing by the track gate.
notes: Coastal Aleppo pine that produces after October downpours; village pickers come early, so weekday mornings are calmest.

name: Puig de Solà
access: From El Perelló take the C-44 north towards El Vendrell and turn off at the lay-by onto the forest track; park at the gate where the pinewood starts.
notes: Dense coastal pine that keeps the morning mist; reliable second-flush ground once the early zones dry out.

name: Obagues del Mont Caro
access: From Roquetes drive up the Mont Caro road, park at the spring below the pass and take the north-face path into the black pines.
notes: High shady pinewood that needs real cold nights; the season peaks in late October and November after the lowlands are finished.

name: Serra del Portell
access: From Roquetes follow the Caro road and branch left onto the forest track at the Portell bend; park at the water tank.
notes: Steady Scots pine that produces after the first September storms; picked hard by Roquetes locals so dawn starts pay off.

name: Costes dels Reguers
access: From Roquetes take the road towards els Reguers and continue on the track past the last olive terraces; park at the turning circle.
notes: Transition belt between Aleppo and Scots pine; best in the week after autumn rain before the weekend foragers arrive.

name: Tossal de les Forques
access: From Ulldecona take the track to the Sant Joan del Pas hermitage; park at the hermitage clearing and climb the pinewood to the north.
notes: Shaded mixed pine above the hermitage that fruits well after September storms; light pressure except on feast days.

name: Serra de Montsià nord
access: From Ulldecona follow the signs to the castle and continue on the crest track; park at the bend below the antennas.
notes: Northeast-facing slopes of the Montsià range holding damp late into the season; quiet midweek and easy to wander.

name: Devesa de Freginals
access: From Freginals take the southern track past the wind-farm gate and follow it into the pinewood; park at the cistern by the bend.
notes: Sheltered west-facing Aleppo stand that does well after wet Septembers; almost nobody picks here on weekdays.

name: Serrat de les Pinedes
access: From Freginals take the road towards Godall and turn onto the first forest track left; park at the gate at the edge of the pinewood.
notes: Modest Aleppo belt that yields only after October storms; very quiet except for the odd local from Godall.

name: Pinyes de Sant Gregori
access: From Batea take the road towards Vilalba dels Arcs and turn onto the forest track at the Sant Gregori sign; park at the cistern.
notes: Roomy plateau pine that rovellons colonise hard after storms; the season starts late, rarely before mid-October.

name: Els Planells
access: From Batea take the C-43 towards Gandesa and turn north on the vineyard track at km 2; park at the track junction.
notes: Open Aleppo flats that need two good storms before producing; wet years bring a memorable November flush.

name: Lo Tossal de Batea
access: From Batea follow the road towards Corbera d'Ebre and take the forest track at the second pinewood; park at the turning by the tank.
notes: Higher mixed pine over clay that holds water well; a quiet corner that few pickers reach before November.

name: Serra de la Pena
access: From Vilalba dels Arcs take the road towards Batea and branch onto the serra track past the vineyards; park at the track gate.
notes: North-facing mixed pine that wakes early for this zone; weekday pressure is minimal.

name: Tossal Redó
access: From Vilalba dels Arcs take the C-43 towards Gandesa and turn off at the olive-grove track; park at the bend where the pinewood starts.
notes: Ordinary Aleppo ground that only produces after solid autumn rain, but then gives spread-out picking.

name: Serrat de llicorella
access: From Torroja del Priorat take the road towards Gratallops and pull onto the vineyard track before the first bend; park at the gate past the last cellar.
notes: Slate-country pine between the vineyards; small but reliable patches after September storms, and tourist traffic keeps it unfished early.

name: Pinedes del Coll de la Teixeta
access: From Torroja del Priorat take the Falset road and turn off at the coll towards Pradell; park at the lay-by on the pass.
notes: Warm open slope that fruits in bursts; check it a week after each storm as the ground dries fast.

name: Solana de Montsant
access: From Poboleda follow the track towards the Escaladei monastery and continue to the firebreak below the cliff line; park at the water deposit.
notes: Big sunny faces of Scots pine that produce after the first cool storms; popular with Priorat locals, so come on weekdays.

name: Coma Fosca
access: From Poboleda take the trail signed to the Montsant springs and leave the path at the second gully; park at the edge of the village.
notes: Shaded gullies that keep moisture through dry spells; the rovellons arrive later but fatter than on the solana.

name: Tossal de les Guàrdies
access: From Sarral take the C-14 towards Montblanc and turn onto the forest track signed to the tossal; park at the end of the track.
notes: Patchy pine over clay that gives good baskets in wet Octobers; light pressure except from Sarral families on Sundays.

name: Serrat de Comaverd
access: From Sarral follow the vineyard road west and take the pinewood track at the water tank; park at the tank.
notes: Open west-facing slope that is quick to fruit after storms and quick to dry — time the visit between rains.

name: Serra del Tallat
access: From Solivella take the road towards Blancafort and branch onto the serra track at the Comabella junction; park at the junction.
notes: Proper Scots pine on the shaded side of the Tallat; a steady producer once the first cold nights arrive.

name: Les Solanes
access: From Solivella take the road towards Sarral and turn off at the pine track before the pass; park at the track gate.
notes: Mixed pine belt with strong rovelló years after wet late summers; Solivella families work it on Sundays.

name: Montmagastre
access: From Tàrrega follow the road towards Guimerà and turn off at the Montmagastre sign; park at the track below the old church.
notes: Dry-land pine around the abandoned settlement; Aleppo rovellons appear after September storms in good years.

name: Serrat del Bosc
access: From Tàrrega take the road towards Bellpuig and turn onto the farm track at the second pinewood; park where the track bends at the wood's edge.
notes: Ordinary Aleppo grove on the plain's edge, only worth a visit in storm autumns when it can surprise.

name: Valls del Corb
access: From Guimerà take the road towards Vallbona de les Monges along the Riu Corb; park at the rest area past the bridge and climb the north slope.
notes: Gorge slopes that keep humidity, so rovellons show with the first storms and the mixed pine stretches the season.

name: Bosc de la Salada
access: From Guimerà take the road towards Tàrrega and turn off at the track to the salt spring; park at the clearing by the spring.
notes: Sheltered southwest wood over clay that fruits after October rain; mostly picked by locals, so go early.

name: Serra Alta
access: From Torregrossa take the road towards Juneda and turn onto the forest track at the serra; park at the gate by the track bend.
notes: Dry Aleppo hillside that only produces after two autumn storms; very quiet and easy walking.

name: Bosc de Vallmajor
access: From Torregrossa take the track towards Vallmajor past the farmland; park at the cistern at the edge of the wood.
notes: Open Aleppo stand on the plain's rim; productive only in wet autumns, when whole families from the village turn up.

name: Serra de la Llena nord
access: From Vinaixa take the road towards Arbeca that climbs la Llena; park at the pass and follow the crest track north.
notes: Dense Scots pine on the shaded side of la Llena; the classic rovelló bank of les Garrigues, busy the weekend after any storm.

name: Serra de la Llena sud
access: From Vinaixa take the road towards el Cogul and turn onto the forest track that climbs the south face; park at the bend by the tank.
notes: Sunny side of la Llena that fruits earlier but dries faster; best a few days after rain, before weekend pressure.

name: Coll de la Llosa
access: From Vinaixa follow the la Llena road to the Coll de la Llosa and take the westward track; park at the coll.
notes: High, damp corner of the serra where the season starts early and lasts; worth the winding drive after August storms.

name: La Llena de Dalt
access: From La Floresta take the track that climbs to the top of la Llena behind the village; park at the water deposit on the crest.
notes: Shady Scots pine near the crest that holds damp well; a dependable early-season bank before the lower pines wake.

name: Costes de la Floresta
access: From La Floresta take the road towards Arbeca and turn onto the forest track at the second bend; park at the lay-by by the pines.
notes: Southeast slopes with mixed pine; good mid-season picking once the crest banks have been worked.

name: Sant Pere el Bigatà
access: From Cervera take the road towards Sant Pere el Bigatà signed from the northern ring road; park at the clearing by the shrine.
notes: The Segarra's best Scots-pine patch; rovellons come with the first September storms and last until the cold.

name: Tossal de Montagut
access: From Cervera take the road towards Tarroja de Segarra and turn onto the forest track at the tossal; park at the track end.
notes: West-facing mixed pine over clay; decent baskets in wet Octobers with light competition.

name: Pinedes d'Ivorra
access: From Guissona take the road towards Ivorra and continue past the village onto the pine track; park at the gate by the bend.
notes: Quiet Scots-pine stands that few outsiders know; produces steadily after the first autumn storms.

name: Els Prats Alts
access: From Guissona take the local road towards Sant Ramon and turn off at the prats; park at the farm gate.
notes: Rolling open pine that fruits in patches; easy family ground with sparse picking pressure.

name: Pla de la Font
area: Gimenells i el Pla de la Font
access: From Gimenells take the road to el Pla de la Font and then the sand track into the pines; park at the clearing by the old corrals.
notes: Deep Segrià Aleppo flats that need September storms to wake; the season here runs late, well into November.

name: Tossal de les Pinyes
area: Gimenells i el Pla de la Font
access: From Gimenells take the track north past the farmland to the tossal; park at the water tank on the shoulder.
notes: A small dry stand that yields only in wet autumns, but nobody else bothers with it.

name: Serra d'Almenar
access: From Almenar take the track up the serra behind the village; park at the reservoir by the first pines.
notes: Segre-side Aleppo pine that produces after October rain; very quiet, with easy walking on soft sand.

name: Costa del Segre
access: From Almenar take the road towards Massalcoreig and turn off at the track above the river; park at the bend overlooking the Segre.
notes: Open pine above the river flats; only productive after stormy autumns, when the moisture lingers in the hollows.

name: Pineda de Les
access: From Les take the signed track above the village that climbs the flank north of the N-230; park at the clearing by the water tank at the edge of the pines.
notes: Cool pinewood that keeps the dew until mid-morning after the Garona fog lifts, so it fruits early in the season.

name: Slopes above Arròs
access: From Les drive east on the N-230 to Arròs and take the forest track behind the last houses; park at the bend where the track enters the pine stand.
notes: Quiet west-facing slope that few locals work, best a couple of days after rain.

name: Solana de Canejan
access: From Canejan take the track that leaves the village towards the upper meadows; park at the barns where the metalled surface ends.
notes: Morning sun warms this bank quickly, so pick here on the early side after a cold front.

name: Umbria de Pruedo
access: From Canejan follow the lane west out of the village and take the forest track rising to the north-facing slopes; park at the track junction by the trough.
notes: Deep shade and moss hold moisture long after rain, making it one of the last productive spots in dry autumns.

name: Pinedes de Benòs
access: From Es Bòrdes take the minor road to Benòs and continue on the dirt track above the hamlet; park at the lay-by at the first bend.
notes: A well-drained bank that produces in flushes after the September rains, with light pressure from Es Bòrdes pickers.

name: North slope above Gua
access: From Es Bòrdes cross to Gua and take the track that climbs behind the houses; park at the gate where the track enters the state forest.
notes: Shaded and mossy, it holds a late crop but the walk keeps most pickers away.

name: Solana d'Arres
access: From Arres take the track that rises from the lower village towards the sunny slope; park at the shrine where the surface worsens.
notes: Fast-drying bank that is only worth it in wet weeks, though it warms up first in October.

name: North slopes above Arres
access: From Arres follow the old lane towards the Hostal de Rius and take the second forest track on the left; park at the culvert.
notes: Mossy pinewood with steady moisture, a reliable spot once the first cold nights arrive.

name: Solana de Vilaller
access: From Vilaller take the lane leaving the N-260 towards the upper barns; park at the first track bend under the pines.
notes: A warm bank that starts producing early, though it dries out fast between storms.

name: Umbría de Vilaller
access: From Vilaller take the path network towards the Barruera road and climb the north-facing bank above the hamlets; park at the roadside before the track forks.
notes: Faces the Boí valley cold airflow and stays damp, good for a second flush in late October.

name: Voltants d'Obarra
access: From Sopeira take the narrow road signed to the Obarra monastery; park at the bend below the monastery and continue on foot up the track.
notes: Sheltered valley that funnels moisture from the Isàvena, so it often fruits when higher slopes are dry.

name: Pineda sobre Sopeira
access: From Sopeira take the track that climbs west of the village towards the ridge; park at the water deposit.
notes: Open stand with scattered flushes of rovelló after storms, but it bakes dry within days.

name: Pinedes d'Ainet de Cardós
access: From Esterri de Cardós take the road to Ainet de Cardós and continue on the track behind the village; park at the barns at the track end.
notes: Classic Cardós pinewood with a good mix of sun and shade, productive from mid-October in wet years.

name: Slope above Arròs de Cardós
access: From Esterri de Cardós drive down to Arròs de Cardós and take the steep track on the valley side; park at the transformer station.
notes: Dense shade keeps the moss wet, and the short steep climb filters out weekend pressure.

name: Serrat de la Costa
access: From Esterri de Cardós take the track that switchbacks up the north wall of the valley; park at the last hairpin before the track dead-ends.
notes: High, mossy belt where the crop comes late but heavily once the first frosts threaten.

name: North slopes above Àreu
access: From Alins follow the road up to Àreu and take the forest track climbing the shaded side of the valley; park at the sawmill clearing.
notes: Rich mixed pine belt in the heart of Vall Ferrera, among the best-producing slopes in the Pallars.

name: Solana d'Alins
access: From Alins take the track that rises behind the church towards the sunny slope; park at the fountain at the edge of the wood.
notes: Warmer bank that starts producing before the high slopes, worth checking in late September.

name: Camí de Norís
access: From Àreu take the rough lane signed to Norís; park at the village and follow the path into the open black pine stands above.
notes: High open stand that only wakes after sustained September rain, but then holds moisture through cold snaps.

name: Plans de Peramea
access: From Peramea take the track that runs along the sunny edge of the plateau; park at the chapel at the village entrance.
notes: Plateau edge that dries fast, so target it right after the first autumn storms.

name: Costa de Baén
access: From Peramea follow the lane towards Baén and continue on the track above the hamlet; park at the bridge before the track climbs.
notes: Quiet corner of the Baix Pallars with light picking pressure and steady crops in moist years.

name: Pi negre de Llessui
access: From Sort take the mountain road to Llessui and continue to the ski station; park at the base buildings and walk into the forest below the pistes.
notes: Famous black pine belt above Llessui that can be crowded on October weekends after a good rain.

name: Serrat del cim de Port Ainé
access: From Sort drive up the Port Ainé station road; park at the antenna gate below the summit and follow the edge of the slopes.
notes: Wind-scoured upper stand that produces in short bursts right before the first snows threaten.

name: Solana sobre Llessui
access: From Sort take the road to Llessui and branch right on the forest track before the village; park at the sheepfold where the track levels.
notes: Sunny side that warms early, often the first high ground to fruit in the comarca.

name: Els Encantats slopes
access: From Espot take the paved park road to the Sant Maurici lake; park at the La Presa gate and walk on towards the Encantats.
notes: Iconic but strictly walk-in ground inside the national park, so pressure is modest despite its fame.

name: Camí d'Amitges
access: From Espot take the paved park road to the Sant Maurici lake; park at the La Presa gate and follow the Amitges trail on foot.
notes: Mossy subalpine pine forest that can give a heavy late crop but demands a long, regulated walk.

name: North slope of Serra de Gurp
access: From Tremp take the road to Gurp and continue on the forest track along the north side of the serra; park at the col where the track forks.
notes: The shaded side of the serra keeps the moss damp and reliably produces after October rains.

name: Solana de la Serra de Gurp
access: From Tremp take the road to Gurp and branch onto the track that traverses the sunny flank; park at the cistern on the bend.
notes: Hot bank with patchy fruiting, best hit two or three days after a storm.

name: Pinedes de Sant Gervasi
access: From Tremp take the road towards Gurp and turn off at Sant Gervasi onto the dirt track behind the hamlet; park at the threshing floor.
notes: Remote and little-picked pinewood that rewards the extra walk in moist autumns.

name: Costa de Llordà
access: From Isona take the road to Llordà and continue on the track below the castle; park at the bend at the edge of the pines.
notes: Ordinary pinewood with modest but regular crops, quiet even on holiday weekends.

name: Vessant de Conques
access: From Isona take the road towards Conques and turn onto the track that climbs the slope west of the village; park at the shrine on the bend.
notes: Open stand on the Conca Dellà edge that fruits early and dries out just as fast.

name: North slope above Llimiana
access: From Llimiana take the track that climbs behind the village to the north-east; park at the reservoir viewpoint where the track narrows.
notes: Shaded slope catching moisture from the Montsec, so it holds a crop longer than the plain.

name: Solana de Llimiana
access: From Llimiana take the lane signed towards the Sant Llorenç reservoir and park at the quarry gate where the pine track starts.
notes: Warm, fast bank that gives a quick first flush after September storms.

name: Solana d'Alòs
access: From Alòs de Balaguer take the track that rises south of the village towards the serra; park at the water tank at the first bend.
notes: South-facing pinewood that fruits in pulses right after rain and empties fast under local pressure.

name: Umbria d'Alòs
access: From Alòs de Balaguer cross the bridge and take the forest track on the shaded side of the valley; park at the hunting post at the track bend.
notes: Cooler and damper than the solana, with a later, steadier crop.

name: Pinedes de Santa Linya
access: From Alòs de Balaguer take the road to Santa Linya and the dirt track behind the village; park at the entrance to the olive terraces.
notes: Transitional pinewood between the plain and the serra that produces best in wet Octobers.

name: Pinedes d'Ivars
access: From Ivars de Noguera take the track that climbs north-east from the village; park at the grain silo where the tarmac ends.
notes: Little-visited pinewood where the moss carpet stays green well into autumn.

name: South slope of Ivars
access: From Ivars de Noguera follow the lane towards the southern fields and take the track into the pines; park at the bend by the hut.
notes: Open stand that needs a good soaking before it produces, but then comes in heavily.

name: Slope above Gerb
access: From Os de Balaguer drive to Gerb and take the paved lane that rises behind the village; park at the cemetery gate where the track begins.
notes: Handy roadside pinewood that takes pressure from Balaguer pickers on Sundays.

name: Pi roger d'Os de Balaguer
access: From Os de Balaguer take the track that traverses the slope towards Gerb; park at the bend overlooking the fields.
notes: Open pine stand with modest but regular fruiting in the first cool weeks of October.

name: Sant Alís summit woods
access: From Àger take the mountain road past Corçà up to the Sant Alís radar station; park at the antenna gate and walk the tracks into the black pine.
notes: High Montsec stand that keeps humidity from the sea fog and produces late in the season.

name: Voltants de Corçà
access: From Àger take the road to Corçà and continue on the forest track towards the crest; park at the bend at the upper meadows.
notes: Wind-exposed open stand where crops appear briefly after the first autumn storms.

name: Plans de Soses
access: From Soses take the track that runs north-east into the pine flats; park at the irrigation hut where the track forks.
notes: Dry Aleppo pine that only wakes after autumn storms, and only for a few days.

name: Pineda sud de Soses
access: From Soses take the farm road south towards the Segre and turn into the pine track; park at the old barn.
notes: Needs a solid two-day rain before it produces, then yields quick flushes in late October.

name: Pinedes de Torres de Segre
access: From Torres de Segre take the paved farm lane north of the village; park at the water pump house at the pine edge.
notes: Easy-access Aleppo pine that dries within days, so time it right after rain.

name: South flats of Torres
access: From Torres de Segre take the track that heads south-west towards the river woods; park at the cattle trough.
notes: Close to Lleida so it gets picked over quickly once word spreads after a storm.

name: Pineda d'Alpicat
access: From Alpicat take the paved track that runs north-west from the village; park at the picnic area at the pine edge.
notes: Morning shade keeps it slightly damper than the plain, but it still needs storm rain to fruit.

name: South slope d'Alpicat
access: From Alpicat take the farm road south towards the highway and turn onto the pine track; park at the transformer hut.
notes: Heavily picked by city foragers in wet autumns, so go on the first fine day after rain.

name: Pinedes d'Alcarràs
access: From Alcarràs take the track north-east past the orchards into the pine stand; park at the well at the field edge.
notes: Ordinary Aleppo pine that gives a short, sharp flush after the first October storms.

name: South pines of Alcarràs
access: From Alcarràs take the farm road south-west to the dryland fields; park at the bend where the pines start.
notes: Very dry stand that only produces in exceptionally wet autumns, but access is trivial.

name: Pinedes de Vallbona
access: From Vallbona de les Monges take the track that climbs east behind the monastery; park at the stone cross at the wood edge.
notes: Transitional pine belt where scots begin to mix in, so crops last longer than on the plain.

name: West slope of Vallbona
access: From Vallbona de les Monges take the lane west towards the Tuixent road and park at the track bend under the pines.
notes: Cooler west flank that keeps storm moisture and produces a second flush in November.

name: Pineda de Belianes
access: From Belianes take the paved farm lane north of the village; park at the chapel at the pine edge.
notes: North-facing Aleppo pine that holds dew, a reliable late-season option for the Urgell.

name: South slope of Belianes
access: From Belianes take the track south towards the stream beds; park at the cistern by the track fork.
notes: Dry open stand that produces only after autumn storms and dries again within a week.

name: Costa de Maldà
access: From Maldà take the lane that rises north-east from the station; park at the barns at the edge of the pines.
notes: Where scots pine starts to take over, the moss holds better and crops stretch later.

name: Solana de Maldà
access: From Maldà take the track south-west above the vineyards; park at the hut where the pine track climbs.
notes: Mixed pine on a warm bank that yields quickly after rain but draws local pickers.

name: Pineda de Barbens
access: From Barbens take the paved lane north towards the Urgell canal; park at the bridge where the pine track starts.
notes: Dew-fed Aleppo pine that produces in short windows after the October canal mists.

name: East pines of Barbens
access: From Barbens take the farm road east towards Ivars and turn into the pine stand; park at the track bend by the hut.
notes: Open dry stand that needs consecutive storm days before it is worth the walk.

name: Pinedes de Juneda
access: From Juneda take the track that climbs north-east from the cooperativa; park at the reservoir above the vineyards.
notes: The best-known Garrigues pinewood, so expect company after the first good rain.

name: South slope of Juneda
access: From Juneda take the lane south-west past the winery and continue on the pine track; park at the stone hut at the bend.
notes: Drier and quieter than the north woods, fruiting briefly after autumn storms.

name: Pineda de l'Espluga Calba
access: From L'Espluga Calba take the track that rises north of the village to the tower; park at the water tank below the crest.
notes: Shaded Aleppo pine on the rim of the depression that keeps moisture better than the plain below.

name: South slope of l'Espluga Calba
access: From L'Espluga Calba follow the lane south-east towards the Vinaixa road; park at the quarry bend where the pines thicken.
notes: Open warm stand that produces only in wet autumns but is rarely picked out.

name: Costa nord de Torà
access: From Torà take the track that climbs the north bank above the village; park at the hermitage at the pine edge.
notes: Scots creep into the Aleppo here, so the moss holds and crops run longer into November.

name: Solana de Torà
access: From Torà take the lane south-east past the swimming pool and into the pine track; park at the cistern on the ridge.
notes: Warm open bank that gives a fast first flush and dries just as quickly.

name: West slope of Torà
access: From Torà cross the bridge and take the dirt track on the west side of the valley; park at the barns where the track steepens.
notes: Dense shaded stand that few walkers reach, holding a steady late crop in moist years.

name: Pinedes de Sant Ramon
access: From Sant Ramon take the track that rises north-west behind the sanctuary; park at the fountain at the wood edge.
notes: A cooler corner of the Segarra where mixed pine keeps the soil damp after rain.

name: East slope of Sant Ramon
access: From Sant Ramon take the farm road east towards Gàver and turn into the pine track; park at the bend by the hut.
notes: Open Aleppo stand that produces in short bursts after the first October storms.

name: Costa d'Estaràs
access: From Estaràs take the lane that climbs the north slope behind the village; park at the track fork under the pines.
notes: North bank with mixed pine and green moss, one of the steadier Segarra spots.

name: Solana d'Estaràs
access: From Estaràs take the track south-west towards the Ferran road; park at the water trough at the field edge.
notes: Dry sunny stand that only fruits after proper autumn rain and stays quiet otherwise.

name: Costa de Sanaüja
access: From Sanaüja take the track that climbs west above the Llobregós valley; park at the shrine at the top bend.
notes: Valley-side moisture and mixed pine make this a solid late-October option.

name: East slope of Sanaüja
access: From Sanaüja take the lane east towards Biosca and turn onto the pine track; park at the barns at the track bend.
notes: Quiet east-facing stand where scots pine mixes in and the crop stretches later than on the plain.

name: Obaga de Fígols
access: From Fígols take the L-401 towards Organyà and turn onto the forest track signed for the Obaga de Fígols; park at the bend below the water tank.
notes: Mossy north-facing pines that hold dew well into the morning, though the near tracks get picked over early in the season.

name: Coll de Jou
access: From Alinyà take the track past the Casa Forestal towards the Coll de Jou; park at the clearing on the col.
notes: Drier south-east slopes that fruit only after good autumn rain and see little picking pressure.

name: Costes de Sant Silvestre
access: From Oliana take the C-14 south and climb the track signed for Sant Silvestre; park at the hermitage gate.
notes: Sheltered slopes above the reservoir that keep moisture from the Segre valley mists and are picked by locals at weekends.

name: Serrat de les Soleies
access: From Oliana cross the Segre bridge and take the track up the Serrat de les Soleies; park at the first bend.
notes: Sun-baked open pine that needs a wet September before it produces, then goes fast under pressure from town.

name: Obaga Moixa
access: From Bassella take the N-260 towards Organyà and turn onto the track for the Obaga Moixa; park at the track barrier.
notes: Cool dense pine on the valley's shady side that fruits reliably after the first October rains.

name: Serrat de Bassella
access: From Bassella take the road up to the Serrat and continue on the forest track; park at the water tank clearing.
notes: Ordinary pine with light pressure, best mid-season once the valley bottom has had steady rain.

name: Obaga del Pui
access: From Cabó follow the valley track towards the head of the Val de Cabó; park at the barrier past the last masies.
notes: Deep mossy obaga where rovellons appear early and stay fresh if autumn mornings are humid.

name: Costa Llarga
access: From Cabó take the track over the shoulder towards the Costa Llarga; park at the bend below the repeater.
notes: Mixed-age pine with moderate local pressure; a good second choice when the obagues are already stripped.

name: Bosc Comunal d'Estamariu
access: From Estamariu take the comunal forest track above the village; park at the turning circle by the hay barns.
notes: Well-kept communal pine with thick moss layers that hold moisture long after rain.

name: Serrat de la Pineda
access: From Estamariu take the minor road towards the Serrat de la Pineda and continue on the dirt track; park at the col.
notes: Ordinary pine belt that yields modestly but sees almost no competition on weekdays.

name: Obaga de Bové
access: From Estamariu take the track down towards the Bové masies and follow the obaga path; park at the first masia.
notes: Cool north-east slope that keeps producing well into late October in damp years.

name: Bosc de Cava
access: From Cava take the track past the upper masies into the Bosc de Cava; park at the forest gate.
notes: Mossy high pine where fruiting starts in late September and stretches through October.

name: Costa Solana
access: From Cava take the road towards Ansovell and turn onto the Costa Solana track; park at the shrine bend.
notes: Warm open slope that only produces after generous rain, with very light picking pressure.

name: Costa de Josa
access: From Josa take the old path towards the Costa de Josa; park at the track gate below the village.
notes: A rich mixed pine belt with thick moss where rovellons fruit in flushes from late September.

name: Serra de Mentid
access: From Tuixén take the forest track along the Serra de Mentid; park at the col above the village.
notes: Local families work these slopes hard at weekends, so an early start matters in wet years.

name: Coll de Pradell
access: From Josa take the track towards the Coll de Pradell; park at the col and work either side.
notes: Quiet high ground that holds a late October crop when lower sectors have already dried out.

name: Bosc d'Aransa
access: From Aransa take the forest track towards the foot of the Serra del Cadí; park at the track gate above the village.
notes: Holiday-country pressure is real here in October, though the mossy patches keep producing after rest days.

name: Obaga de Meranges
access: From Meranges take the track past the Cadí viewpoint; park at the Caseta de Meranges and climb into the obaga.
notes: Steep shady black pine that fruits late and heavily in wet autumns but is walked by Puigcerdà pickers at dawn.

name: Solana de Meranges
access: From Aransa take the eastern track towards the Meranges solana; park at the spring below the slope.
notes: Sunnier mixed pine that needs a proper rainy spell, then delivers for a short window before the crowds.

name: Foresta de La Molina
access: From La Molina take the road towards Fontanals de Cerdanya and park at the forest parking by the first bend; walk the woods behind.
notes: Piste-edge pine that gets busy with ski-town visitors on fine October weekends.

name: Coma Piosa
access: From La Molina take the forest track into the Coma Piosa; park at the clearing at the track end.
notes: Dense high black pine with excellent moss that fruits into November in cool autumns.

name: Coll de Pal
access: From La Molina take the road up to the Coll de Pal; park at the col and drop into the woods on the shady side.
notes: Late ground above 1600 m that only pays off from late October into November.

name: Santa Maria de Talló
access: From Bellver de Cerdanya take the local road to Santa Maria de Talló; park below the church and work the pine flats behind.
notes: Easy family ground that is picked over quickly, though it re-fruites after each rainy week.

name: Solana de Talló
access: From Talló take the track up the solana towards the serra; park at the cistern clearing.
notes: Dry open Scots pine that produces only in genuinely wet autumns, with modest pressure.

name: Serrat de Vilallobent
access: From Puigcerdà take the N-152 towards Llívia and turn off to Vilallobent; park at the edge of the village.
notes: So close to Puigcerdà that dawn patrols from town strip the first flush, but the mossy strip along the stream keeps going.

name: Obaga de Vilallobent
access: From Vilallobent take the dirt track towards the obaga; park at the hay barns at the track end.
notes: Dense pine that holds dew from the Segre plain and rewards mid-week visits once the weekend crowd is gone.

name: La Carrerada
access: From Puigcerdà take the N-152 to Llívia and follow the signs for the Carrerada path; park where the track leaves the northern edge of town.
notes: The classic town walk gets heavy pressure on holiday mornings, so it is best at first light after rain.

name: Serra d'Avitlladora
access: From Llívia take the road towards Estavar and turn onto the track for the Serra d'Avitlladora; park at the col by the water tank.
notes: Shady north-west pine above the exclave that fruits steadily through October despite busy weekend traffic.

name: Costa de la Tor
access: From La Tor de Cerdanya take the forest track towards the Bosc de la Coma; park at the fountain above the village.
notes: Village-side slope picked by families after school hours, so morning visits find the best flushes.

name: Obaga del Cadí
access: From La Tor take the track climbing towards the Cadí north face; park at the barrier at the forest edge.
notes: Steep shady ground below the Cadí cliffs that stays humid late into autumn.

name: Serrat de Sanavastre
access: From Das follow the road to Sanavastre; park by the church and walk the pines behind the village.
notes: Small but reliable Scots pine flats that local families know well; expect company on Sundays.

name: Bosc de Das
access: From Das take the track into the Bosc de Das north of the village; park at the picnic area.
notes: Ordinary pine that produces acceptably after two or three days of steady autumn rain.

name: Prat de Cadí
access: From Montellà follow the PR trail towards the Prat de Cadí; park at the track gate above Martinet and climb on foot.
notes: The long walk keeps pressure low, and the high plateau holds a late October-November crop of clean rovellons.

name: Serrat del Prat de Cadí
access: From Montellà take the Cadí footpath to the serrat above the Prat; park at the same gate and continue past the plateau.
notes: Very quiet high black pine where fruiting waits for late October and the first snows can cut the season short.

name: Refugi de Malniu
access: From Lles de Cerdanya take the signed track to the Malniu lakes; park at the Refugi de Malniu.
notes: The popular lakes circuit means steady footfall, but the mossy black pine either side keeps producing.

name: Estanys de Malniu
access: From Lles take the track past the Cap del Rec ski centre; park at the centre and follow the lakes circuit on foot.
notes: Open high ground that only fruits from late October, when cool damp weather settles over the serra.

name: Cap del Rec
access: From Lles de Cerdanya drive the paved road to the Cap del Rec ski centre; park at the base hut and work the woods beside the pistes.
notes: One of the richest black pine belts in the area, though weekend skiers-turned-pickers comb the near pines.

name: Estany de Lanós
access: From Lles take the track towards the Estany de Lanós; park at the gate below the Prat de Lanós and continue on foot.
notes: Quiet high circuit that holds moisture from the lake and fruits into November.

name: Serrat de Lanós
access: From Lles take the western forest track towards the Serrat de Lanós; park at the track end clearing.
notes: Late high ground that rewards patient pickers once the lower Cerdanya woods have dried out.

name: Estanys de la Pera
access: From Meranges take the track to the Estanys de la Pera; park at the barrier below the first lake.
notes: A classic but demanding circuit that fruits from late October, with clean crops after the first cold rains.

name: Solana de la Pera
access: From Meranges take the eastern track signed for the lower Pera lakes circuit; park at the track gate.
notes: Sunnier side of the basin that needs a wet spell, then produces briefly before the season closes.

name: Tosa d'Alp
access: From Alp take the road up to the Masella resort; park at the cable-car base and climb the ridge woods.
notes: Ski-resort woods that see plenty of October visitors, so the further from the lift the better.

name: Bosc de la Masella
access: From Alp take the GIV-404 to the Masella base station; park at the La Pleta parking and walk the forest road.
notes: Dense piste-side pine that keeps dew until mid-morning and re-fruites quickly between busy weekends.

name: Sant Sebastià de Molló
access: From Molló take the track towards the Sant Sebastià chapel; park at the chapel clearing.
notes: Village shrine woods with steady but polite pressure; best after the first week of October rain.

name: Obaga del Ritort
access: From Molló take the forest track up the Vall del Ritort; park at the gate past the last houses.
notes: Cool valley-head pine that holds moisture late and sees mostly local pickers.

name: La Serra
access: From Sant Pau de Segúries take the track towards La Serra; park at the water depot.
notes: Open roadside pine that produces lightly but is a safe bet on damp mornings close to town.

name: Obaga de la Pineda
access: From Sant Pau take the track climbing to the Obaga de la Pineda; park at the bend above the pastures.
notes: Mossy north slope that carries good flushes in wet years and is walked mostly by villagers.

name: Coma Frecha
access: From Les Llosses follow the forest track into the Coma Frecha; park at the track barrier.
notes: Hidden valley pine with almost no pressure and reliable moisture in the comas.

name: Serra de Mermider
access: From Les Llosses take the track along the Serra de Mermider; park at the col by the transmitter.
notes: Ordinary pine belt that yields modest baskets after sustained autumn rain.

name: Serrat de les Creus
access: From Les Llosses take the western track to the Serrat de les Creus; park at the track end.
notes: Quiet west-facing ground where rovellons linger into early November.

name: La Pineda
access: From Ripoll cross to the left bank of the Freser and take the track past La Pineda; park at the chapel.
notes: So close to town that early risers clear the near pines, but it re-fruites after every rainy spell.

name: Serrat de Terrades
access: From Ripoll take the track towards the Serrat de Terrades; park at the quarry bend.
notes: Open pine with light crops in dry years, best visited mid-week when pressure is low.

name: Refugi de Coma de Vaca
access: From Queralbs take the Camí de Núria and branch up the Coma de Vaca trail; park at the Queralbs station car park.
notes: A long walk keeps picking pressure minimal, with a late October-November season in the high black pine.

name: Costa de les Agudes
access: From Queralbs follow the Sant Jaume path and climb towards the Costa de les Agudes; park at the station car park.
notes: Exposed high slopes that fruit briefly but generously once cold damp weather settles in.

name: Els Bacives
access: From Setcases take the mountain road up to the Vallter 2000 resort; park at the base station and walk the slopes below the Bacives ridge.
notes: Resort-side black pine with steady weekend pressure; the far side of the ridge is quieter and fruits later.

name: Obaga del Ter
access: From Setcases follow the road towards Vallter and park at the last hairpin below the resort; drop into the obaga on foot.
notes: Sheltered valley-head pine that holds moisture from the Ter and produces into November.

name: Vall de Núria
access: From Ribes de Freser park at the rack-railway station and take the Cremallera to the sanctuary of Núria; the valley paths start at the top station.
notes: Busy sanctuary valley where the near woods are picked daily, but the upper paths keep late flushes.

name: Costes del Puigmal
access: From Ribes de Freser park at the station and take the Cremallera rack railway to Núria, then follow the Puigmal path south-east from the sanctuary.
notes: Very high ground that only fruits from late October, when clean cold rains finally reach the upper pines.

name: Pla de Sant Segimon
access: From Vallfogona de Ripollès take the road up to the Santuari de Sant Segimon; park at the sanctuary and walk the plateau pines.
notes: Sanctuary plateau with mixed pine that families work gently; best after the first fortnight of October.

name: Serrat de la Balma
access: From the Sant Segimon sanctuary take the forest track north-west to the Serrat de la Balma; park at the track gate below the plateau.
notes: Dense high pine that keeps a late crop when the valley woods have already been picked through.

name: Sant Pere d'Albanyà
access: From Albanyà take the track past the Sant Pere d'Albanyà monastery; park at the old bridge.
notes: Cool gorge-side pine where autumn humidity from the Fluvià keeps the moss damp.

name: Serra de Bestracà
access: From Albanyà take the track towards the Serra de Bestracà; park at the Coll de Bestracà.
notes: Open Mediterranean-facing pine that needs heavy September rain before it produces at all.

name: Santa Bàrbara de Pruneres
access: From Oix take the track towards the Santa Bàrbara de Pruneres chapel; park below the chapel.
notes: West-facing chapel woods with light pressure and a short but productive season after storms.

name: Costa Llarga de Montagut
access: From Montagut take the road towards Oix and park at the track bend above the village; the Costa Llarga path starts there.
notes: Low warm pine that fruits erratically and is mostly worked by locals on Sundays.

name: Sant Martí de Sales
access: From Sales de Llierca take the track past Sant Martí de Sales; park at the churchyard.
notes: Dense north pine in a quiet corner of the Alta Garrotxa with dependable autumn moisture.

name: Costa del Castellot
access: From Sales de Llierca take the eastern track to the Costa del Castellot; park at the turning by the masies.
notes: Little-visited slope where rovellons appear late in the season if October stays mild.

name: Sant Miquel de Falgars
access: From Les Preses take the road up to Sant Miquel de Falgars; park at the sanctuary car park and walk the pines on either side.
notes: Easy access means weekend families pick the near woods, but the northern band behind the sanctuary holds up.

name: Els Colls
access: From Les Preses take the road towards Falgars and continue on the forest track to Els Colls; park at the track gate.
notes: Open sunny pine over the Bas valley that produces well only in wet autumns.

name: El Garrix
area: La Vall de Bianya · Sant Salvador
access: From Sant Salvador de Bianya take the track towards El Garrix; park at the first group of houses.
notes: Quiet north-facing pine with a small but steady crop in ordinary years.

name: Coll de Capsacosta
area: La Vall de Bianya · Sant Salvador
access: From Sant Salvador de Bianya take the road towards the Coll de Capsacosta; park at the col.
notes: Breezy open ground at the head of the valley that fruits briefly after the first proper rains.

name: Obaga de Sant Jaume
access: From Sant Jaume de Frontanyà take the BV-4243 north and then the forest track signed to the Peguera stream; park at the clearing by the water tank.
notes: Sheep-grazed obaga that holds moisture late into the season, but fruitbodies stay small and are quickly taken by local pickers.

name: La Peguera
access: From Sant Jaume de Frontanyà follow the minor road up the Peguera valley; park at the trackside space beside the shrine bend.
notes: North-east slopes that fruit steadily after autumn rains, with moderate pressure concentrated at weekends.

name: Serrat del Mig
access: From Sant Jaume de Frontanyà take the footpath climbing the north-west ridge beyond the last farmhouses; park at the village edge.
notes: High and quiet, it needs a wet week before it produces, but rovellons stand here late into November.

name: Comes de la Nou
access: From La Nou de Berguedà take the forest track up behind the church towards the spring; park at the turning circle below the font.
notes: Mossy hollows keep humidity well and picking pressure stays low midweek.

name: El Solell
access: From La Nou de Berguedà follow the lane south-east past the last masies; park at the gate of the final enclosure.
notes: A warmer, drier face that fruits only after good October rains and empties fast on fine weekends.

name: Obagues del Castell
access: From Castell de l'Areny take the steep lane up towards the castle ridge; park at the track junction below the ruins.
notes: Deep, shaded slopes where rovellons appear early, though thin soils mean baskets fill slowly.

name: Terrades
access: From Castell de l'Areny follow the valley track down to the east; park at the concrete ford.
notes: Ordinary pine with light pressure, best in the first cold weeks of November.

name: Obac de Sant Julià
access: From Sant Julià de Cerdanyola take the B-400 towards Borredà and turn onto the forest track; park at the picnic area.
notes: Cool north-facing pinewood that produces reliably after the first October storms.

name: Els Sales
access: From Sant Julià de Cerdanyola take the farm lane south-west past the last masies; park at the open gate by the transformer hut.
notes: A mixed, sunnier stand that yields only in damp autumns and sees mostly local pickers.

name: Mirador de Cerc
access: From Cerc take the BV-4241 north and pull in above the reservoir; park at the viewpoint lay-by.
notes: Ordinary pine on stony ground, worth a visit only when the lower woods have already dried out.

name: Obaga de Cerc
access: From Cerc follow the track into the obaga behind the village; park at the water deposit.
notes: Mossy and shady with modest pressure, giving steady if never abundant picks.

name: Obac de Sagàs
access: From Sagàs take the minor road towards the Llobregat valley and turn up the forest track; park at the bend by the cattle grid.
notes: A quiet, sheep-grazed obac where rovellons appear late but stand untouched midweek.

name: El Soleu de Sant Andreu
access: From Sagàs take the lane south-east past Sant Andreu de Sagàs; park at the trackside below the church.
notes: Warm south-east-facing slopes that need sustained rain before they fruit at all.

name: Obaga d'Olvan
access: From Olvan take the road towards La Coromina and then the forest track; park at the quarry gate.
notes: Damp north-west woodland close to Berga, so expect company on holiday weekends.

name: Riera d'Olvan
access: From Olvan take the C-16 frontage road down to the riera bridge; park at the wide verge before the track.
notes: Low, open pine along the stream that fruits only after very wet Octobers and is picked over within days.

name: Costa de Montclar
access: From Montclar de Berguedà take the lane climbing to the northern crest; park at the last farmhouse before the track.
notes: A forgotten, mossy belt that produces quietly every season thanks to low visitor numbers.

name: Les Solanes
access: From Montclar de Berguedà follow the farm track south-east past the telecommunications tower; park at the wide bend.
notes: Ordinary pine on the sunny side, best checked early in the season after the first rains.

name: Obaga de Fígols
access: From Fígols take the BV-4243 towards Saldes and turn onto the track at the col; park at the col's pull-in.
notes: Old mining country where the shaded slopes still hold good moisture and pressure is moderate.

name: Coll de Fígols
access: From Fígols take the old road towards Cercs; park at the bend below the col.
notes: A modest, south-west stand that yields in waves after each rainy spell.

name: Obagues d'Avià
access: From Avià take the B-422 north and turn onto the forest track; park at the water tank clearing.
notes: Close to Berga and busy on Sundays, with small but regular flushes.

name: Serrat d'Avià
access: From Avià follow the paved lane west past the last houses; park at the field gate.
notes: Dry, open pine that only produces in exceptionally wet autumns.

name: Comaflora
access: From Gósol take the road towards Josa and then the track into the Serra del Verd; park at the foot of the Comaflora track.
notes: A high, mossy black-pine comal that holds snowmelt dampness and fruits heavily once the season turns.

name: Les Solanelles
access: From Gósol follow the track climbing the south-east flank of the Serra del Verd; park at the fold below the crest.
notes: Sun-baked upper slopes that only produce after a wet, cold spell and see almost no pickers.

name: Obagues del Verd
access: From Gósol take the long footpath up to the north-west crest of the Serra del Verd; park where the track ends at the forest limit.
notes: Late, cold-country rovellons that stand well into December if autumn rains have been generous.

name: Obaga de Clariana
access: From Clariana de Cardener take the C-55 towards Solsona and turn onto the forest track; park at the bend by the pylon.
notes: A compact obaga near the Cardener that yields steadily and absorbs weekend pressure well.

name: Els Plans de Clariana
access: From Clariana de Cardener follow the farm road south-west onto the plateau; park at the grain silo.
notes: Ordinary plateau pine, productive only in wet years and mostly after the first cold nights.

name: Obac de la Molsosa
access: From La Molsosa take the lane north-west past the last mas; park at the end of the tarmac.
notes: A remote, damp obac where baskets fill slowly but surely and you rarely meet another picker.

name: El Solei de la Molsosa
access: From La Molsosa follow the track south past the church; park at the ford.
notes: Southern exposures that stay dry unless autumn is rainy, then fruit briefly and heavily.

name: Sant Climenç
access: From Pinell de Solsonès take the road to Sant Climenç and continue on the forest track; park below the village.
notes: Rolling pine around Sant Climenç with light pressure and modest, regular flushes.

name: Els Plans del Pinell
access: From Pinell de Solsonès follow the local road south-east; park at the track junction by the cemetery.
notes: Ordinary pine on gentle slopes that needs back-to-back rains to produce.

name: Obaga de Riner
access: From Riner take the C-452 towards Solsona and turn onto the track at kilometre 4; park at the wide bend.
notes: Mossy north-east slopes that produce after every decent autumn storm.

name: Els Plans de Riner
access: From Riner take the farm road west towards the Cardener flats; park at the bridge.
notes: Low, open stands with thin picks except in exceptionally wet autumns.

name: Serrat de les Farges
access: From Sallent take the C-16 service road towards the Llobregat and climb the track at the Serrat de les Farges; park at the water tank.
notes: Weekend pressure from the Bages belt means early mornings pay off after rain.

name: El Solei de Sallent
access: From Sallent follow the road up the southern flank towards the tower; park at the quarry lay-by.
notes: Warm slopes that fruit late and only after a genuinely wet October.

name: Castelladral
access: From Navàs take the B-430 towards Castelladral and continue on the forest track; park below the church.
notes: A shady, little-visited pinewood that keeps moisture well into November.

name: El Solei de Navàs
access: From Navàs take the road south-east past the station; park at the level crossing.
notes: Ordinary pine with easy access, picked over quickly by town families on Sundays.

name: Serrats d'Avinyó
access: From Avinyó take the BV-4315 towards Artés and turn onto the track; park at the crest bend.
notes: Small but regular flushes on the northern serrats, best midweek to avoid weekend crowds.

name: El Solei d'Avinyó
access: From Avinyó follow the paved lane south past the last houses; park at the vineyard gate.
notes: Easy-access southern pine that yields only in damp years and is heavily combed on holidays.

name: Costa de Montserrat
access: From Sant Vicenç de Castellet take the BV-4241 towards Marganell and pull in at the bend below the Montserrat wall; park at the lay-by.
notes: Low Aleppo belt where rovellons appear briefly after storms before the weekend crowd clears them.

name: Riera de Castellet
access: From Sant Vicenç de Castellet take the path up the riera from the station; park at the bridge.
notes: Riverside pine that only produces after very wet spells and sees constant local traffic.

name: Santa Cecília
access: From Marganell take the BP-1103 towards Monistrol and turn off to Santa Cecília; park at the monastery car park.
notes: Heavily walked Montserrat foothill pine where anything showing is gone by mid-morning.

name: Cova de Marganell
access: From Marganell follow the track south past the hermitage; park at the fountain.
notes: Busy, dry southern slopes that produce only after abundant rain and are combed daily in season.

name: Cingles de Marganell
access: From Marganell take the rough track up the north-east cliff country; park at the track end below the cingles.
notes: Steep and crowded Montserrat spurs where damp pockets can still surprise early risers.

name: Sant Miquel
access: From Monistrol de Montserrat take the camí to the Sant Miquel hermitage; park at the road's end above the town.
notes: The most hammered north face in the massif — dawn starts are essential for even a small basket.

name: Sant Joan
access: From Monistrol de Montserrat follow the trail towards Sant Joan; park at the first hairpin of the mountain road.
notes: Constant foot traffic means rovellons here are found only in the days right after rain.

name: Camí dels Apòstols
access: From Monistrol de Montserrat take the camí dels Apòstols up the western flank; park at the cemetery gate.
notes: Pilgrim paths keep these woods picked clean, though damp autumns still bring brief flushes.

name: Sant Martí del Castell
access: From Castellcir take the track past Sant Martí del Castell; park below the church.
notes: A cool, mossy obaga of the Moianès plateau with steady production and few pickers.

name: Obagues de Castellcir
access: From Castellcir follow the lane south-west down to the riera; park at the ford.
notes: Ordinary pine near the stream that fruits well after wet weeks and stays quiet midweek.

name: Sant Joan d'Oló
access: From Santa Maria d'Oló take the road to Sant Joan d'Oló and continue on the forest track; park at the village edge.
notes: Damp north-west woods around Sant Joan that produce dependably through October.

name: Els Plans d'Oló
access: From Santa Maria d'Oló follow the lane south-east onto the plans; park at the grain store.
notes: Sunny plateau pine that needs repeated rains before the first rovellons show.

name: Obac de Sant Agustí
access: From Sant Agustí de Lluçanès take the track north past the last masies; park at the water deposit.
notes: A quiet, elevated obac that holds autumn dampness and fruits well into November.

name: El Solei de Sant Agustí
access: From Sant Agustí de Lluçanès follow the lane south past the church; park at the bend.
notes: Southern exposures, dry until good October rains, then productive for a short window.

name: Obaga d'Oristà
access: From Oristà take the track climbing north from the football pitch; park at the field corner.
notes: Deep mossy pine near the head of the valley, reliable and largely unpicked.

name: Els Plans d'Oristà
access: From Oristà follow the farm road south-west towards the plateau; park at the track junction.
notes: Ordinary pine on gentle plans that produces only after sustained autumn rain.

name: Serrat d'Oristà
access: From Oristà take the lane north-east to the serrat above the village; park where the tarmac ends.
notes: A cool ridge shoulder where late-season rovellons linger after the lower woods finish.

name: Obac del Grau
access: From Sant Bartomeu del Grau take the road towards Oristà and turn onto the forest track; park at the picnic table.
notes: Shaded, undisturbed pinewood that keeps moisture and rewards patient searching.

name: El Solei del Grau
access: From Sant Bartomeu del Grau follow the lane south-east down the valley; park at the old mill.
notes: Warmer slopes that fruit briefly after storms and see mostly local traffic.

name: Serra de Bellmunt
access: From Seva take the road up towards the Serra de Bellmunt; park at the track junction below the antenna.
notes: Popular weekend wood for Barcelonans, so expect pressure and go early after rain.

name: El Solei de Seva
access: From Seva take the C-17 frontage road and climb the south-east lane; park at the bend above the town.
notes: Sun-facing pine close to the road that empties fast on fine autumn Sundays.

name: Cingles de Sau
access: From Vilanova de Sau take the road past the reservoir dam and climb to the cliff footpaths; park at the mirador.
notes: Damp cliff-country pine above the pantà, scenic and busy, with good post-rain flushes.

name: Sant Romà de Sau
access: From Vilanova de Sau follow the lane towards Sant Romà; park where the road dips to the cove.
notes: Around the drowned church the woods are walked constantly, so only early birds fill baskets.

name: Obac d'Osormort
access: From Sant Sadurní d'Osormort take the C-25 side road and turn onto the forest track; park at the col.
notes: Mossy Guilleries-edge pine that produces well and still escapes the worst crowds.

name: El Solei d'Osormort
access: From Sant Sadurní d'Osormort follow the lane south past the church; park at the bridge over the riera.
notes: Ordinary southern pine, productive only in wet autumns and picked by locals daily.

name: Castell d'Orís
access: From Orís take the track up to the castle ruin; park at the farm gate below.
notes: A quiet north-west obac below the Castell d'Orís that holds moisture late.

name: Serrat d'Orís
access: From Orís take the lane south-east along the serrat; park at the transformer hut.
notes: Easy-access pine near the road, swept quickly on holiday weekends.

name: Sant Segons
access: From Viladrau take the forest track up the northern flank of the Turó de l'Home; park at the track end below Sant Segons.
notes: High Montseny slopes with big, cold-country rovellons but constant weekend pressure.

name: Les Guelles
access: From Viladrau take the long path up the north-west face towards the summit plateau; park at the gate on the summit road.
notes: Mossy subalpine pine that fruits heavily after the first frosts but is walked by crowds from the summit road.

name: Font del Gat
access: From Viladrau take the track east from the summit road junction; park at the spring clearing.
notes: East-flank pine where damp gullies give steady picks despite heavy Montseny footfall.

name: Matagalls Nord
access: From Viladrau drive up to Coll Formic and take the Matagalls path north; park at the col.
notes: The classic Matagalls north face — productive but picked over by the army of dawn hikers.

name: Matagalls Est
access: From Viladrau take the track from Coll Formic towards the south-east shoulder; park at the fence corner.
notes: Less steep than the north face but still busy, with flushes right after each rainy spell.

name: Matagalls Ponent
access: From Viladrau take the western path up from the Fontmartina side; park where the track forks below the ridge.
notes: Western slopes facing Fontmartina see steady traffic, so late arrivals find only scraps.

name: Serrat del Molló
access: From Peralada take the GIV-602 toward Vilabertran and turn onto the serrat track; park at the gate below the ridge.
notes: Ordinary pine stands that only fruit well after steady September rain, with light local picking pressure.

name: Serra de Rodelles
access: From Peralada take the road toward Vilanant and continue on the forest track at the serra foot; park at the turning circle by the water tank.
notes: Open groves that dry out fast, so go early in the season before the October heat waves.

name: Solà de Sant Quirze
access: From Rabós follow the track to the Sant Quirze de Colera monastery; park at the bend below the sunny slope.
notes: Quiet Albera slopes where the banks hold moisture late into November if the autumn storms arrive.

name: Bacs de la Coma Freda
access: From Rabós take the Albera track west from the village and climb toward the north-facing hollows; park at the track fork under the pines.
notes: Shady north bacs that stay damp long after rain, but the steep ground means few pickers and slow walking.

name: Serrat de la Falguera
access: From Rabós take the minor road toward Cantallops and then the gravel track up the serrat; park at the clearings by the old charcoal platform.
notes: A little-picked corner where production depends on late-September thunderstorms rolling in from the Gulf of Lion.

name: Puig Ventós
access: From Avinyonet take the track that climbs to the puig from the north side of the village; park at the reservoir clearing below the summit.
notes: Dry inland Aleppo pine that needs a wet week before it produces, and the crop rarely lasts past mid-November.

name: Serrat de les Comes
access: From Avinyonet take the C-252 toward Llers and turn onto the serrat track; park at the bend by the olive terraces.
notes: Open stands on thin soil that fruit briefly but are close enough to Figueres to be picked over by weekenders.

name: Coll de Lli
access: From Agullana take the GI-601 toward La Vajol and continue on the coll track; park at the clearing at the pass.
notes: Cool north slopes near the French border that keep their moisture and often run a week later than the plain.

name: Solans d'Agullana
access: From Agullana take the track below the village on the Sant Climent side; park at the farmhouse gate by the second bend.
notes: Sunny-slope pines that produce only in damp autumns and see steady traffic from Figueres on Sundays.

name: Bac Gran de Cantallops
access: From Cantallops take the forest track behind the village toward the north-east hollows; park at the spring below the bac.
notes: Dense shady stands that hold dew well, though wine-country day-trippers thin the easy strips near the track.

name: Serrat de les Roses
access: From Cantallops take the road toward Espolla and turn onto the serrat track; park at the cistern clearing on the ridge.
notes: Moderate cover where finding rovellons depends on catching the first rain after a dry spell.

name: Serrat de Sant Dalmau
access: From Llers take the local road toward Sant Dalmau and continue on the serrat track; park at the chapel clearing.
notes: Low open groves on the Empordà plain edge that only produce after properly wet Octobers.

name: Coma Seca
access: From Llers take the track south-west from the village toward the dry hollow; park at the bend by the dry-stone wall.
notes: As the name says the ground drains fast, so any flush is short and picked within days of the rain.

name: Serra Nord de Garriguella
access: From Garriguella take the Vilamaniscle road and turn onto the serra track; park at the cistern on the north ridge.
notes: Wine-village slopes where the pines are dry and the rovellons appear only in genuinely wet autumns.

name: Coll de Mates
access: From Garriguella take the track toward Rabós past the vineyards and climb to the coll; park at the track bend below the pass.
notes: Open sunny slopes close to the coast road that get combed over by locals on All Saints weekend.

name: Sant Joan de Salelles
access: From Quart take the GIV-6021 up to the Salelles chapel and continue on the forest track; park at the chapel clearing.
notes: First pines of the Gavarres north edge, heavily worked by Girona pickers the weekend after each rain.

name: Costes de Malanyit
access: From Quart take the track from the Creu de Quart bend toward the Gavarres; park at the fire-break gate above the vineyards.
notes: Dense west-facing slopes where the moss holds dew and the rovellons run later than the open ridges.

name: Serrat de Sant Sebastià
access: From Celrà take the track up past the Sant Sebastià hermitage; park at the hermitage gate and walk the ridge north.
notes: Gavarres front slopes with easy Girona access, so the wide trackside strips are picked clean by Sunday noon.

name: Comes Altes
access: From Celrà take the GI-632 toward Juià and turn onto the track at the quarry bend; park at the quarry apron.
notes: Open stands that dry quickly, productive only when the tramuntana lets the autumn rains settle in.

name: Serrat de les Coves
access: From Sant Julià de Ramis take the road past the Caves of the Serres and follow the serrat track; park at the cave parking.
notes: Pine flats above the Ter gorge that get steady Girona pressure the morning after each rain.

name: Turó del Montdellà
access: From Sant Julià de Ramis take the track from the Meder river bridge toward the north-facing hill; park at the track end gate.
notes: Dense shady slopes that keep their moisture and hide unpicked pockets a short walk from the road.

name: Serres de la Creu del Ter
access: From Sant Julià de Ramis cross the Ter bridge and take the first forest track on the right; park at the bend by the pylon.
notes: Open serres overlooking the Ter that produce in bursts and are quickly stripped by after-work pickers.

name: Serrat del Pedró
access: From Madremanya take the GIV-6431 toward Sant Martí Vell and turn onto the serrat track; park at the track gate above the village.
notes: Golden-stone village slopes with moderate picking pressure and good crops when September is stormy.

name: Solana de Madremanya
access: From Madremanya take the track west past the last houses and follow the contour path; park at the water deposit clearing.
notes: West-facing groves that fruit early and short, worth the first week after the opening rains.

name: Puig de Cadiretes
access: From Tossa take the GI-681 toward Lloret and turn off at the Cadiretes track; park at the coll below the puig.
notes: The highest ground of the massif holds dew on its north face, but Lloret and Tossa pickers sweep it every weekend.

name: Serra de Can Carboner
access: From Tossa take the old Vidreres road and climb the serra track at the second bend; park at the fire-tank clearing.
notes: Open coastal pine that needs two good rains to produce, then gives a fast, heavily contested flush.

name: Costes de Puig Figuer
access: From Tossa take the Sant Grau road and stop at the bend below Puig Figuer; park at the picnic-area lay-by.
notes: Sunny coastal slopes with easy parking, so anything within sight of the road is gone by ten in the morning.

name: Serrat del Pedró d'Anglès
access: From Anglès take the GI-534 toward Sant Hilari and turn onto the Guilleries track at the Segueró bend; park at the track fork.
notes: Proper mossy Scots pine belt that fruits reliably after the first autumn rains and sees only local pickers.

name: Solà del Ter
access: From Anglès take the track along the Ter toward the falls and climb at the marked path; park at the angling club car park.
