notes: Moderate cover on the Guilleries fringe where the season stretches into December in wet years.

name: Turó de Sant Jaume
access: From Maçanet take the track behind the industrial estate toward the turó; park at the chapel clearing on the hill.
notes: A busy Girona-and-coast midpoint, so the near groves are thin and the far side of the turó is where to walk.

name: Serra Sud de Maçanet
access: From Maçanet take the Caldes road and turn onto the serra track at the slaughterhouse bend; park at the water tank.
notes: Open mixed pine that gives modest crops most years and is heavily worked on October Sundays.

name: Serrat del Morer
access: From Sils take the road toward Maçanet and turn onto the serrat track at the cattle farm; park at the field gate.
notes: Low pine on the edge of the wetlands that fruits only after damp, windless autumns.

name: Turó dels Camps
access: From Sils take the track west from the station quarter and climb the turó; park at the bend by the antenna.
notes: Open groves with light yields but almost no competition on weekday mornings.

name: Sant Pere del Bosc
access: From Lloret take the GI-682 up to the Sant Pere del Bosc sanctuary; park at the sanctuary car park.
notes: Heavily picked urban woodland where any flush disappears within a day of the rain.

name: Turó dels Muladers
access: From Lloret take the road toward Tossa and stop at the lay-by below the turó; park at the bend and take the path up.
notes: Roadside coastal pine with constant pressure from town pickers, so go at dawn the morning after rain.

name: Castell de Solterra
area: Sant Hilari · Sant Miquel de Solterra
access: From Sant Hilari take the GIV-5201 toward the sanctuary of Sant Miquel de Solterra; park at the castle ruins and follow the north path.
notes: Classic mossy Guilleries Scots pine that fruits steadily from October, though the castle clearing itself is well known.

name: Pla del Boix
area: Sant Hilari · Sant Miquel de Solterra
access: From Sant Hilari take the Vilanova de Sau road and turn onto the Guilleries track at the Osor sign; park at the boix clearing.
notes: Deep Guilleries ground where the mist keeps the moss wet and the season runs long into late autumn.

name: Serrat del Cau
area: Sant Hilari · Sant Miquel de Solterra
access: From Sant Hilari take the track toward can Cassasses from the reservoir road; park at the gate on the serrat's south side.
notes: Quiet Scots pine belt a long walk from the sanctuary crowds, productive for those who know the fire-breaks.

name: Serra de Vulpellac Sud
access: From Vulpellac take the track toward the Gavarres edge past the castle; park at the track gate by the olive groves.
notes: Gavarres south-west pine that does best in wet Mays and Septembers, with steady weekend pressure from the coast.

name: Serrat de Sant Sadurní
access: From Forallac take the road toward Peratallada and turn onto the serrat track; park at the chapel of Sant Sadurní.
notes: Open slopes above the golden villages that fruit briefly and are combed by locals each October.

name: Serra Nord de Corçà
access: From Corçà take the track up from the Rupià road toward the Gavarres; park at the bend by the water deposit.
notes: North-east slopes that catch the sea damp and give reliable early crops in most autumns.

name: Bacs de Casses
access: From Corçà take the road toward La Bisbal and turn onto the forest track at the Kilometre 2 marker; park at the track widening.
notes: West-facing bacs close to La Bisbal, so expect company from mid-morning onwards on holidays.

name: Puig de l'Alarma
access: From Vall-llobrega take the track behind the village toward the Gavarres ridge; park at the firing-range gate.
notes: The first serious climb above the plain holds damp north faces that fruit well after sea-fog nights.

name: Solana del Palau
access: From Vall-llobrega take the Palau-sator road and turn onto the solana track; park at the bend below the pines.
notes: Sunny coastal-dry groves with Palamós weekenders on every track, worth only the first days after rain.

name: Montplà
access: From Torroella take the road toward the Montgrí castle and branch left on the Montplà track; park at the castle trail junction.
notes: Coastal-dry massif where rovellons appear only after exceptional autumn rain and never last long.

name: Serra del Montgrí Sud
access: From Torroella take the Ullà track past the church and climb the east flank; park at the quarry bend.
notes: Dry east-facing pine above the rice plain, combed by town pickers despite its modest yields.

name: Serra Nord de Mont-ras
access: From Mont-ras take the track toward the Pals hills past the campsite; park at the cistern clearing on the ridge.
notes: Quiet pine above the coast plain that produces in wet autumns and is usually left to locals.

name: Solana de l'Escletxa
access: From Mont-ras take the road toward Pals and turn onto the solana track at the second bend; park at the vineyard gate.
notes: Open dry groves close to the beaches, so weekend pressure is high even though crops are thin.

name: Serrat de la Mata
access: From Porqueres take the road toward Banyoles along the lake's south side and turn onto the serrat track; park at the farm gate.
notes: Lake-side slopes with good autumn dew, picked over by Banyoles walkers every Sunday.

name: Serrat de Miava
access: From Porqueres take the track toward Mata and continue past the ponds to the serrat; park at the cattle grid.
notes: Moderate pine belt where the season opens early and the easy paths go first.

name: Serrat Alt
access: From Serinyà take the track toward the C-66 pass and climb the north-east slope; park at the quarry lay-by.
notes: Pine above the Banyoles fault with steady moisture from the north-east and only moderate pressure.

name: Coma Torta
access: From Serinyà take the road toward Cornudella and turn onto the west track; park at the bend by the dry-stone hut.
notes: Open groves that give quick short flushes and are usually quiet on weekday mornings.

name: Serrat Roig
access: From Crespià take the track north from the village toward the serrat; park at the spring below the ridge.
notes: Quiet inland pine on red soil that fruits well after September storms and sees few outsiders.

name: Solana Sud
access: From Crespià take the Esponellà road and turn onto the south track at the chapel; park at the track end.
notes: South-facing slopes that need a soaking before they produce, but then hold a late-October crop.

name: Serrat de la Torre
access: From Calella take the BV-5024 toward Hortsavinyà and turn onto the serrat track; park at the fire-tank clearing.
notes: Deep Montnegre north slopes where the sea damp helps, but Barcelona plates appear from Saturday dawn.

name: Turó de les Agudes
access: From Calella take the road toward Santa Susanna and climb the forest track at the campsite; park at the track gate.
notes: Open coastal pine above the resorts, stripped by town pickers within a day of any rain.

name: Coll d'Hortsavinyà Sud
access: From Calella take the Hortsavinyà road and stop at the coll below the ruined village; park at the coll lay-by.
notes: Busy coll woodland where the crop is thin and the parking spots fill before nine at weekends.

name: Turó de la Creu d'Ardaca
access: From Òrrius take the BV-5005 toward Vilanova del Vallès and turn onto the turó track; park at the crossroads clearing.
notes: Corredor foothills that open the Maresme season early and draw Barcelona pickers each Sunday.

name: Serrat de les Fonts
access: From Òrrius take the track from behind the church toward the south-east serrat; park at the fountain on the lower path.
notes: Moderate groves near the springs that keep damp and get picked in waves all through October.

name: Sota el Castell de Burriac
access: From Cabrera de Mar take the BV-5024 to the Burriac castle car park; park there and take the north path below the walls.
notes: The castle slopes are the classic Maresme spot, so expect heavy pressure the morning after every rain.

name: Serra d'Aguir
access: From Cabrera de Mar take the road toward Vilassar de Dalt and turn onto the serra track; park at the water deposit.
notes: Open pine near the transmission masts where yields are modest and the Maresme crowds pass through anyway.

name: Montnegre Sud
access: From Tordera take the GI-602 toward Hortsavinyà and turn onto the Montnegre track; park at the park-information gate.
notes: The south gateway to Montnegre, worked by both Maresme and Girona pickers on autumn weekends.

name: Serra Est del Riu Tordera
access: From Tordera cross the river bridge and take the first forest track on the east bank; park at the sports-field end.
notes: River-damp pine that opens early, and the near groves are gone before the weekend.

name: Serrat de Sant Daniel
access: From Tordera take the Palafolls road and turn onto the serrat track at the chapel; park at the track end below the ridge.
notes: Open ground a long walk in, which keeps some rovellons on the table after the road-edge flush is gone.

name: Serrat de la Pedra Negra
access: From Sant Vicenç de Montalt take the BV-5024 toward Dosrius and turn onto the serrat track; park at the picnic area.
notes: Corredor foothills with easy access from the coast road, so the picnic-area groves are picked clean by Sunday.

name: Solana de Sant Vicenç
access: From Sant Vicenç de Montalt take the track above the golf course toward the south-east slope; park at the course gate.
notes: Sea-facing slopes that need wet Septembers and get constant golf-club traffic in the season.

name: Carena de la Serralada de Marina
access: From Teià take the BV-5002 up to the Coll de Can Borrell and park at the coll; walk the carena north of the road.
notes: The most pressured woodland in the Maresme, with Barcelona pickers out before sunrise after every rain.

name: Turó dels Cells
access: From Teià take the road toward Alella and turn onto the turó track by the vineyards; park at the track bend.
notes: Open pine between the vineyards and the crest where any flush is short and instantly picked.

name: Serra Nord de Sant Pol
access: From Sant Pol take the road up from the train station toward the chapel and continue on the serra track; park at the chapel.
notes: Sea-damp north-east slopes that fruit after foggy weeks but are swept by village pickers every morning.

name: Pinedes de la Punta d'en Racó
access: From Sant Pol take the coast track toward Calella and climb west at the first bend; park at the cove lay-by.
notes: Coastal dry pine above the coves where crops are small and never survive the weekend.

name: Turó de la Guàrdia
access: From Piera take the forest track behind the cemetery towards the Turó de la Guàrdia; park at the track gate before the pines close in.
notes: Dew lingers on the north face until mid-morning, though Sunday walkers from the village thin the pickings early.

name: Pineda de Can Ferrer
access: From Piera take the BV-2243 towards Sant Sadurní and turn onto the Can Ferrer dirt track; park at the bend where the track narrows.
notes: Dry southwest slopes that only produce after a solid week of autumn rain, so time your visit behind the first October storms.

name: Serra de la Figuera
access: From Piera follow the paved lane towards La Figuera and continue on the forest track; park at the clearing by the water tank.
notes: A mossy northeast belt that carries moisture late into the season and still yields baskets after the crowds have moved to Montserrat.

name: Turó de la Corona
access: From Òdena take the track up towards the Turó de la Corona behind the industrial estate; park at the wide shoulder where the pines start.
notes: West-facing slopes drain fast, so pick here only in the days right after rain while the shaded hollows are still damp.

name: Serra d'Òdena
access: From Òdena take the rural lane towards the Serra d'Òdena farms and continue on foot up the fire track; park at the last farm gate.
notes: Quiet local woods with little pressure, but the southeast exposure means the season here is short and front-loaded.

name: Cinglera de Capellades
access: From Capellades take the path up the cinglera behind the paper mills; park at the car park at the base of the cliff path.
notes: The shady cliff base stays humid well into November, though local pickers from town work it every damp weekend.

name: Coves del Tambor
access: From Capellades take the road towards the Coves del Tambor park; park at the picnic area car park by the caves.
notes: Easy-access pine that gets swept quickly, so it is only worth a dawn stop on the first damp morning after rain.

name: Castell de Claramunt
access: From La Pobla take the signposted track up to the Castell de Claramunt; park at the bend just below the castle ruins.
notes: The northwest slope above the castle holds moisture nicely, but the short walk means it is picked most weekends.

name: Serra Grossa
access: From La Pobla take the lane towards Serra Grossa past the vineyards and follow the fire break track; park at the cistern.
notes: Open southern pines that need a wet autumn to produce, and even then the best banks are bare by ten o'clock.

name: Torre de Cabrera
access: From Cabrera d'Anoia take the track towards the Torre de Cabrera; park at the clearing below the old tower.
notes: A modest northeast stand that gives small but clean flushes when the September rains arrive on time.

name: Serrat de Cabrera
access: From Cabrera d'Anoia take the forest track west towards the Serrat; park at the fork where the track bends uphill.
notes: Far enough from the road to escape casual pickers, though the southwest aspect burns off moisture within days of rain.

name: Camí de Sant Miquel
access: From El Bruc take the Camí de Sant Miquel towards Montserrat; park where the cobbled path leaves the last houses.
notes: Montserrat's south face dries fast, so the window after rain is short and legions of Barcelona pickers hit it at first light.

name: Can Maçana
access: From El Bruc take the C-55 towards Can Maçana; park in the lay-by at the Can Maçana bend by the fountain.
notes: Classic busy ground: the pine banks near the pass are stripped by mid-morning on any damp autumn weekend.

name: Cingles de Montserrat
access: From El Bruc follow the GR-4 towards the Montserrat cliffs; park at the track barrier above the olive terraces.
notes: A steep hour's climb keeps the casual crowd away, but the south-facing conglomerate slopes only hold mushrooms for a few days after rain.

name: Sant Jaume Sesoliveres
access: From Santa Margarida de Montbui take the lane towards Sant Jaume Sesoliveres; park at the shrine and take the north track.
notes: Mossy north banks around the hamlet that produce steadily through October when the Anoia plain is already drying out.

name: Turó de Montbui
access: From Santa Margarida de Montbui take the track up the Turó de Montbui behind the church; park at the reservoir fence.
notes: Open east-facing pines with light pressure, best on the second flush in late October once the early crowd has passed.

name: Serra de l'Atalaia
access: From Sant Sadurní take the road towards Subirats and turn onto the Atalaia forest track; park at the bend by the antenna track.
notes: Low Penedès pine that only fruits after generous autumn rain, and the cava-town crowd picks it hard on damp Sundays.

name: Vilarnau
access: From Sant Sadurní take the road towards Valldeforma and turn off at the Vilarnau lane; park at the edge of the vineyards.
notes: Warm open slopes between vines that give a brief late-season window once the first cold nights arrive.

name: Castell de Miralles
access: From Sant Llorenç d'Hortons take the track towards the Castell de Miralles; park at the plateau below the ruins.
notes: Dense north-facing pine around the castle keeps its humidity, and the distance from town keeps weekend pressure moderate.

name: Serra d'Hortons
access: From Sant Llorenç d'Hortons take the rural road up the Serra d'Hortons past the farmhouses; park at the water deposit.
notes: Ordinary southeast pine that fruits in bursts; go two or three days after rain rather than the morning after.

name: Serra de Font-rubí
access: From Font-rubí take the track along the Serra towards the telecommunication mast; park at the saddle where the track crests.
notes: The highest and dampest corner of the Penedès pine belt, with mossy banks that can carry right into December.

name: Costa de Gunyoles
access: From Font-rubí take the road down towards Gunyoles and turn onto the forest track; park at the shrine by the bend.
notes: Sheltered southwest banks that fruit well in wet years but shut down quickly during dry autumns.

name: Els Clots de Font-rubí
access: From Font-rubí follow the lane north past the last masies to the Clots; park at the turning circle at the track end.
notes: Shaded hollows that keep moisture long after the open slopes have dried, though local families know every clump.

name: Serra de Llorenç
access: From Llorenç del Penedès take the track up the Serra behind the village; park at the gas pipeline pylon.
notes: Low quiet woods where a north-facing gully can hold a late flush when the rest of the comarca has given up.

name: Costa de Sant Miquel
access: From Llorenç del Penedès take the rural road towards Sant Miquel and continue on the dirt track; park at the vineyard margin.
notes: Open dry pine that produces only in genuinely wet autumns, and then just for the first few days.

name: Turó del Castell
access: From Sant Jaume dels Domenys take the lane up to the castle hill; park at the track gate below the walls.
notes: A modest northeast slope that village pickers sweep on Sundays but which re-fruits quietly midweek after rain.

name: Les Comes
access: From Sant Jaume dels Domenys take the road towards el Papiolet and turn onto the Comes track; park at the olives.
notes: Very dry southern pine; only worth a look at the tail end of an exceptionally rainy October.

name: Costa de l'Arboç
access: From l'Arboç take the track up towards the Serra north of town; park at the bend by the old lime kiln.
notes: North-facing Aleppo pine that holds the sea humidity on damp mornings and sees only light local pressure.

name: Serrat de Pedregós
access: From l'Arboç take the road towards Castellet and turn onto the Pedregós track; park at the pull-in by the pines.
notes: Open stony southeast slopes that fruit briefly but heavily in the first wet week of the season.

name: Turó de la Bisbal
access: From La Bisbal del Penedès take the lane up the Turó behind the village; park at the track barrier at the pine edge.
notes: A small north-facing wood that stays productive a few days longer than the surrounding dry slopes.

name: Serra de la Bisbal
access: From La Bisbal del Penedès take the rural road west towards the Serra; park at the shrine on the crest road.
notes: Dry open pine with almost no pressure, a fallback spot only when the wetter hills are already picked over.

name: Les Roquetes
access: From Sant Pere de Ribes take the road up towards Les Roquetes and continue on the forest track; park at the water tank.
notes: Metro-adjacent pine that the Sitges and Ribes crowd strips by mid-morning, so only a dawn visit pays.

name: Solanes de Ribes
access: From Sant Pere de Ribes take the track towards the Solanes above Can Lloses; park at the quarry barrier.
notes: Slightly further in than the Roquetes banks, but still busy on weekends whenever autumn damp settles in.

name: Campdàsens
access: From Garraf village take the BV-2411 towards Olivella and turn off at the Campdàsens track; park at the farm gate.
notes: Karstic Garraf pine that only fruits after real rain, and the city crowd arrives by nine on the first good Sunday.

name: Mirador del Garraf
access: From Garraf village take the road up past the old station towards the C-31; park at the lay-by below the mirador.
notes: Easy-access coastal pine that is swept constantly, worth only the first hours after autumn storms off the sea.

name: Serra d'Ordal
access: From Corbera de Llobregat take the forest track towards the Serra d'Ordal; park at the spring below the pass.
notes: The Ordal range is the metro's favourite mushroom hill; expect company from dawn and a picked-clean understory by noon.

name: Puig d'Agulles
access: From Corbera de Llobregat take the track towards the Puig d'Agulles; park at the fire track junction at mid-slope.
notes: The far side of the Ordal sees slightly less pressure, but southwest exposure shortens the productive window after rain.

name: Turó del Padró
access: From Corbera de Llobregat take the lane west past the last houses to the Padró track; park at the bend by the pines.
notes: Ordal moisture plus steady suburban picking means only the steep western banks still hide unpicked groups.

name: Montpedrós
access: From Cervelló take the road up towards Montpedrós and continue on the forest track; park at the shrine on the shoulder.
notes: A commuter-belt classic that is clean by eight on autumn Saturdays, though north-east banks re-fruit after each rain.

name: Costa de Cervelló
access: From Cervelló take the track south-west above the cemetery; park at the clearing where the pine opens out.
notes: Dry open slopes with moderate pressure that only produce in the wettest weeks of the season.

name: Serra de Marina sobre Pomar
access: From Badalona take the BV-5002 up towards Coll de la Conreria and turn off at the Pomar track; park at the reservoir fence.
notes: Marina woods are picked to the bone by nine a.m. on any damp weekend, so this is strictly a first-light stop.

name: La Conreria
access: From Badalona take the BV-5002 to Coll de la Conreria; park at the old seminary gate and take the forest trail south.
notes: Dense mossy pine close to a million people: superb habitat, zero respite, dawn only and expect empty baskets by ten.

name: Santuari de Puiggraciós
access: From Castellar del Vallès take the road to the Santuari de Puiggraciós; park at the sanctuary car park.
notes: The pine banks around the sanctuary are a Vallès fixture and get heavy weekend pressure all through October.

name: Bosc de Can Febrera
access: From Castellar del Vallès take the Llitera track north into the Can Febrera woods; park at the forest track barrier.
notes: Dense north-facing mixed pine that holds moisture well, though the Granollers crowd knows it as well as anyone.

name: Serra de Sentmenat
access: From Sentmenat take the track up the Serra behind the castle; park at the bend by the water deposit.
notes: Suburban Aleppo pine that gets a steady dusting of local pickers, fruiting only in genuinely damp autumns.

name: Castell de Sentmenat
access: From Sentmenat take the lane up to the Castell de Sentmenat; park at the track gate below the tower.
notes: Easy access means these dry open pines are swept early; useful only on the first morning after good rain.

name: Costa de Can Rector
access: From Caldes de Montbui take the road towards Sant Feliu and turn onto the Can Rector track; park at the farmhouse gate.
notes: Mossy northeast pine in the thermal-spring hills: good habitat but a commuter crowd that arrives with head torches.

name: Serra de Canyelles
access: From Caldes de Montbui take the track up the Serra de Canyelles towards the ridge; park at the fire tank.
notes: The north ridge holds autumn damp for days and is far enough from parking to keep some unpicked ground.

name: Turó del Castell
access: From Sant Feliu de Codines take the lane up to the castle hill; park at the fence at the top of the paved section.
notes: High Vallès pine that starts late and lasts long, though the village's own pickers work the near banks weekly.

name: Solanes de Caldes
access: From Sant Feliu de Codines take the road towards the Caldes road and turn onto the Solanes forest track; park at the col.
notes: Cool northwest solanes that stay damp into December, ideal for the second flush once early pressure fades.

name: Sant Elies
access: From Cànoves take the road up towards Sant Elies; park at the chapel and follow the forest track north-east.
notes: Montseny's south-west flank keeps good humidity here, but the Granollers weekend tide reaches even these paths.

name: Serrat de la Tosca
access: From Cànoves take the Samalús road and continue on the Tosca track; park at the saddle where the track forks.
notes: A long walk filters out most pickers, and the north serrat can hold mushrooms through the whole of a wet November.

name: Costa de Samalús
access: From Cànoves take the road to Samalús and turn onto the Costa track; park at the bend above the stream.
notes: Lower Samalús slopes that fruit early in the season and are largely finished once the Montseny heights start.

name: Turó del Corredor
access: From Llinars del Vallès take the BV-5101 towards the Corredor; park at the Coll de can Bordoi and climb the north path.
notes: The north slopes below the Corredor summit are classic Vallès ground; expect lanterns on the path well before sunrise.

name: Pla de les Arenes
access: From Llinars del Vallès take the BV-5101 to the Pla de les Arenes; park at the picnic area and take the north-east trail.
notes: Easy parking makes the Pla a magnet for families, so the near pines are bare while the far banks still produce.

name: Vall d'Olzinelles
access: From Sant Celoni take the road towards Olzinelles into the Montnegre core; park at the farm at the valley head.
notes: Deep Montnegre valley humidity gives a long season here, and the walk in keeps all but determined pickers away.

name: Costa de la Torre
access: From Sant Celoni take the Olzinelles road and branch left at the Torre track; park at the track end by the stream.
notes: A quiet southeastern flank of Montnegre that produces reliably but only rewards those willing to walk the full hour in.

name: Serra de Bonastre
access: From Bonastre take the track up the Serra behind the village; park at the bend by the disused cistern.
notes: Low-pressure Gaià-country pine where northeast banks can hold a steady trickle of groups through late October.

name: Costa del Coll de la Marca
access: From Bonastre take the road towards the Coll de la Marca and turn onto the forest track; park at the col.
notes: Open slopes near the coll that dry quickly, so pick the first damp mornings after the season's opening rains.

name: Turó de la Riera
access: From La Riera de Gaià take the lane up behind the church to the Turó; park at the water tank at the pine edge.
notes: A quiet corner of the Gaià valley where the northeast slope keeps enough damp for a modest late-season flush.

name: Costa de la Gaià
access: From La Riera de Gaià take the road down the valley and turn onto the Costa track; park at the shrine on the bend.
notes: Very dry coastal-influence pine; worthwhile only in exceptionally wet autumns when the whole valley fruits at once.

name: Fontscaldes
access: From Valls take the road to Fontscaldes and continue on the forest track past the last houses; park at the fountain.
notes: The pine above the spa village holds autumn moisture well, and local pressure is steady but not overwhelming.

name: Masmolets
access: From Valls take the TV-2442 towards Masmolets; park at the hamlet and take the track south-west up the slope.
notes: Out-of-the-way woods where the southwest aspect means a short but rarely contested window after each rain.

name: Serrat Alt
access: From Valls take the road towards Nulles and turn onto the Serrat Alt forest track; park at the fire break gate.
notes: The highest and dampest pine around Valls: north banks here keep producing after the lower country has dried out.

name: Serra de Nulles
access: From Nulles take the lane up the Serra behind the cooperative cellar; park at the track barrier at the crest.
notes: Modest, quiet woods where the north face gives small clean flushes that few people bother to pick.

name: Costa de Nulles
access: From Nulles take the rural road south-east past the vineyards; park at the margin where the pines begin.
notes: Dry open pine between vines that only fruits after proper autumn storms, and even then just for days.

name: Turó de Montferri
access: From Montferri take the track up behind the village to the Turó; park at the bend below the rocky summit.
notes: The pine on the Gaià-side hill catches the sea humidity, giving regular October flushes with light picking pressure.

name: Vall del Gaià
access: From Montferri take the road down to the Gaià valley and turn onto the riverside track; park at the old mill.
notes: Shaded valley pine that keeps damp surprisingly long, though the far banks need a wet fortnight to switch on.

name: Turó del Castell
access: From Rodonyà take the lane up to the castle hill above the village; park at the gate at the top of the lane.
notes: Small quiet north-facing wood that yields steadily in damp years and sees hardly any weekend traffic.

name: Costa de Rodonyà
access: From Rodonyà take the rural road south-east towards the Gaia municipal boundary; park at the track fork.
notes: Open southeast pine that fruits briefly; best treated as a backup when the Alt Camp hills are still dry.

name: Els Estrets del Nord
access: From Alfara de Carles take the track towards the Ports del Nord; park at the barrier before the Estrets gorge.
notes: Shady gorge mouths keep dew well into October and pressure stays low because few pickers walk in from Alfara.

name: Serra de les Molleres
access: From Alfara de Carles follow the forest track that climbs north-west under the Ports cliffs; park at the turning circle below the Molleres meadows.
notes: High damp north faces hold moisture late into autumn but the climb is steep and only fit pickers get up here.

name: La Cabra Foradada
access: From Alfara de Carles take the eastern track towards the Roquetes boundary; park at the clearing by the water tank.
notes: Dense pinewaters on the shady side fruit reliably after the first September storms and see very little picking pressure.

name: El Bac de Pauls
access: From Pauls take the path that drops into the Bac valley; park at the track junction just past the last houses.
notes: The deep north-facing bac keeps humidity all season and rovellons run weeks later than on the Ebre lowlands.

name: Les Comes de Dalt
access: From Pauls take the road towards Cinta and then the forest track east; park at the fold below the first pine bench.
notes: East-facing comas warm early so the season starts soon after August rains, with only local families picking.

name: Serra de Tivenys
access: From Tivenys take the track that climbs the serra behind the village; park at the bend where the pine belt starts.
notes: Aleppo rovellons here come in flushes after September storms and the season often runs well into December.

name: Barranc Fondo
access: From Tivenys take the northern track towards the Benimussa slopes; park at the small clearing at the barranc head.
notes: The shady barranc floor stays damp after rain but thorny access and steep ground keep most pickers away.

name: Serra de Santa Bàrbara
access: From Santa Bàrbara take the lane that rises south-east onto the serra; park at the water depot on the crest.
notes: Open Aleppo woodland fruits only after proper autumn storms, but the flat crest makes for easy family picking.

name: Els Colls
access: From Santa Bàrbara take the road towards Freginals and turn onto the forest track; park at the col by the pines.
notes: A quiet corner where locals find rovellons late in the season once the Godall massif has had rain.

name: Tossal de la Galera
access: From La Galera take the short track up to the tossal behind the village; park at the foot of the antenna track.
notes: South-facing open pines need storm rain before they fruit, and the easy stroll makes it a Sunday family spot.

name: L'Obra
access: From La Galera take the lane north-east towards the old farm of L'Obra; park at the trackside by the ruin.
notes: Sheltered north-east slopes hold the morning dew and late-season rovellons appear after November showers.

name: Slope towards Godall
access: From Mas de Barberans take the track that climbs north towards the Godall range; park at the gate below the pine bench.
notes: A mixed pinewood where the first Scots rovellons of the season appear, well before the high Ports flush.

name: Les Muntelles
access: From Mas de Barberans follow the GR 7 towards the southern Ports; park where the track ends at the boundary stone.
notes: Dense high woodland on the Ports fringe keeps moisture beautifully but demands a long walk and early start.

name: Fontcalda
access: From Bot take the road down to the Fontcalda sanctuary and continue on foot along the Canaletes; park at the sanctuary clearing.
notes: River-valley pines fruit after storm rain and the sanctuary path sees enough visitors that early mornings pay off.

name: Serra de Paüls
access: From Bot take the northern track towards Paüls; park at the bend where the serra flattens into pine woodland.
notes: The north-west serra holds damp after the October storms and remains almost unpicked except for Bot locals.

name: Tossal Roig
access: From La Pobla de Massaluca take the track south-west up the tossal; park at the field edge below the crest.
notes: Sparse Aleppo cover means rovellons only after decent storms, but the open ground makes finding them easy.

name: Serra de la Pobla
access: From La Pobla de Massaluca take the northern lane along the serra; park at the track junction by the pine stand.
notes: Shaded slopes facing the Ebre gorge keep moisture longer and quietly produce into December.

name: Serra de Caseres
access: From Caseres take the track that rises west along the serra towards the Aragón border; park at the clearing on the crest.
notes: West-facing pines dry fast so time your visit right after September storm fronts pass through.

name: Vall Major
access: From Caseres take the lane down into the Vall Major and continue on the forest track; park at the old pond.
notes: The sheltered valley bottom stays humid and rovellons here often survive the whole late-autumn season.

name: Els Estrets
access: From Prat de Comte take the track towards the Estrets gorge; park at the barrier by the abandoned terraces.
notes: Cool gorge heads near the Ports fringe give one of the earliest and most dependable rovellón runs in the Terra Alta.

name: Serra de la Solsida
access: From Prat de Comte take the southern track along the serra; park where the track narrows at the pine line.
notes: A mixed stand that produces late-season flushes when the higher Ports zones are already finished.

name: Sant Gregori
access: From El Pinell de Brai take the lane up to the Sant Gregori sanctuary; park at the sanctuary esplanade.
notes: Sheltered slopes around the sanctuary hold dew well and the easy access means it gets picked hard on free weekends.

name: El Paga
access: From El Pinell de Brai take the western track towards the Paga slopes; park at the bend below the pine bench.
notes: East-facing woodland away from the village stays unpicked and fruits well after the October storms.

name: Serra de Móra
access: From Móra d'Ebre take the lane that climbs the serra behind the town; park at the reservoir viewpoint.
notes: Open south-east pines give a short but generous flush after each storm and draw pickers from the whole town.

name: Barranc de la Casa Nova
access: From Móra d'Ebre take the northern track past the olive groves; park at the head of the barranc by the cistern.
notes: North-facing banks keep the ground damp and locals guard these pines for the late November flush.

name: Serra Llarga
access: From Flix take the road towards la Palma d'Ebre and turn onto the serra track; park at the col by the pines.
notes: The long north-west crest mixes pine types and reliably carries rovellons a week after autumn storms.

name: Tossal de la Vinya
access: From Flix take the eastern track towards the Riba-roja boundary; park at the old vineyard terrace.
notes: Open slopes fruit only in wet autumns but the short walk makes it a classic evening run for Flix pickers.

name: Serra de la Torre
access: From Riba-roja d'Ebre take the track that climbs the serra north-west; park at the bend below the tower ruin.
notes: Dry south-west faces need storm rain, but when it comes the rovellons appear in tight rings and go fast.

name: Costa de l'Aspre
access: From Riba-roja d'Ebre take the lane towards Vinebre and turn up the costa track; park at the pine edge.
notes: Sheltered north-east slopes hold moisture from the river haze and quietly fruit deep into December.

name: La Albarca
access: From Cornudella de Montsant take the road towards La Albarca; park at the hamlet and follow the forest track east.
notes: Transition woodland between Montsant and Prades that gives steady rovellons after the first cold rains.

name: Siurana Slopes
access: From Cornudella de Montsant take the road up to Siurana; park at the reservoir dam and climb the north track.
notes: Popular weekend country under Siurana's cliffs, so go on a weekday if you want the shady north benches.

name: Montsant North Face
access: From Cornudella de Montsant follow the GR 171 into the Montsant; park at the track end below the monastery wall.
notes: Dense shady Scots pine on the famous north face holds moisture all autumn but weekend pressure is heavy.

name: Serra de Falset
access: From Falset take the track that climbs the serra behind the cooperative; park at the water tank on the crest.
notes: Close enough to town for after-work picking, so the first flush after storms disappears within days.

name: Els Camins
access: From Falset take the road towards Marçà and turn onto the eastern forest track; park at the bend by the pines.
notes: Quieter east-facing woodland where late-season rovellons keep appearing after November rains.

name: Serra de Gratallops
access: From Gratallops take the track that rises north above the vineyards; park at the pine belt where the track ends.
notes: North faces above the Priorat vineyards fruit well after storms, and wine-country visitors keep pressure modest.

name: Coll de Gratallops
access: From Gratallops take the lane towards Torroja and climb the coll track; park at the col by the dry-stone hut.
notes: Open south-east ground dries quickly so the season is short and best right after September storms.

name: Montsant West
access: From Ulldemolins follow the track into the Montsant Natural Park; park at the barrier at the park boundary.
notes: Classic weekend Montsant: strong flushes after autumn rain but you must be up early to beat the Reus pickers.

name: Santuari de Montsant
access: From Ulldemolins take the road to the Mare de Déu de Montsant sanctuary; park at the sanctuary gate.
notes: Scots pine around the sanctuary gives dependable October rovellons and sees steady weekend traffic.

name: Coma de Margalef
access: From Ulldemolins take the lane towards Margalef and turn onto the coma track; park at the first bend in the pines.
notes: A sheltered coma away from the main Montsant paths where rovellons linger after the sanctuary slopes are stripped.

name: Serra de la Vilella
access: From La Vilella Alta take the track that climbs north-east above the village; park at the pine edge by the cistern.
notes: North-east slopes catch the morning dew and give a steady second flush when other Priorat zones dry out.

name: Montalt Slopes
access: From La Vilella Alta follow the path towards the Montalt ridge; park where the lane ends at the olive terraces.
notes: Higher, damper woodland under Montalt that fruits late and is usually left to the village regulars.

name: Sant Antoni
access: From Porrera take the lane up to the Sant Antoni hermitage; park at the hermitage and walk into the pines.
notes: The hermitage slopes are a local classic, so after-storm flushes are picked over within a couple of days.

name: Els Colls de Porrera
access: From Porrera take the track north-west towards the colls; park at the col by the turning circle.
notes: A quieter side of Porrera where the mixed pinewood keeps producing after the first cold snaps.

name: Serra de Comaverd
access: From Montblanc take the road towards Rojals and turn onto the Comaverd track; park at the bend below the crest.
notes: North-east faces above the town hold dew and give Montblanc families their first rovellons after storm rain.

name: Serra del Tallat
access: From Montblanc take the road towards Poblet and turn onto the Tallat track; park at the col near the shrine.
notes: The windy Tallat crest dries fast, so the season is short but the easy track access makes it a popular run.

name: Riba de la Conca
access: From Montblanc take the lane towards the Riba stream; park at the small bridge at the pine edge.
notes: Low open Aleppo woodland that only fruits after wet autumns, with easy access close to town.

name: Montargull
access: From Llorac take the road to the hamlet of Montargull; park at the hamlet and follow the track north.
notes: Cool northern woodland near the Segre divide that keeps moisture and fruits steadily through October.

name: Rauric Slopes
access: From Llorac take the lane towards Rauric and turn up the forest track; park at the fold below the pines.
notes: South-west slopes around Rauric give quick flushes after storms and see only a handful of local pickers.

name: Belltall
access: From Passanant take the road to the Belltall hamlet; park by the church and follow the track up the north-west slope.
notes: High, shaded ground near Belltall holds autumn damp and gives one of the latest rovellón runs in the comarca.

name: Colls de Passanant
access: From Passanant take the eastern track towards the Guialmons boundary; park at the col by the pine stand.
notes: East-facing colls warm early, so the season starts ahead of the rest of the Conca after August storms.

name: Serra de Barberà
access: From Barberà de la Conca take the track that climbs the serra north of the village; park at the water tank.
notes: North faces above the Conca hold the dew and rovellons appear within a week of the first good storms.

name: Vall de la Conca
access: From Barberà de la Conca take the lane towards Montblanc and turn onto the eastern valley track; park at the bridge.
notes: A sheltered valley side that keeps producing after the windier crests have dried out.

name: El Cim de Forès
access: From Forès take the track to the top of the serra; park at the track end below the summit pines.
notes: One of the highest and dampest pine benches in the Conca, with a late season that runs to first frost.

name: El Pla de Forès
access: From Forès take the lane east onto the plateau; park at the small clearing by the track bend.
notes: The quiet plateau around the village sees only local pickers and fruits well after October rain.

name: Coll de Mollerussa
access: From Alforja take the road towards Prades to the Coll de Mollerussa; park at the col and follow the north track.
notes: The Prades road brings weekend pickers, so the north benches go fast after every storm.

name: Serra d'Alforja
access: From Alforja take the southern track along the serra; park at the bend where the pine belt thickens.
notes: South-west slopes away from the road stay unpicked and give a late flush after November showers.

name: Muntanyes de Prades
access: From Arbolí take the track that climbs into the Prades massif; park at the barrier at the upper forest edge.
notes: Dense high Scots pine above Arbolí holds moisture all autumn but the walk keeps all but serious pickers away.

name: Costes de Baix Camp
access: From Arbolí take the lane south-east towards the Siurana reservoir; park at the first bend in the pines.
notes: Lower, sunnier Scots pine that fruits early and gives Arbolí families their first taste of the season.

name: Farena
access: From Mont-ral take the road down to the Farena hamlet; park by the bridge and climb the southern track.
notes: The warm Brugent valley side starts early and the hamlet regulars pick it hard on free mornings.

name: La Cadeneta
access: From Mont-ral take the track towards La Cadeneta; park at the track end and follow the path into the dense pines.
notes: Shady north-west woodland deep in the Prades high country where rovellons grow big and pressure stays low.

name: El Pla de Mont-ral
access: From Mont-ral follow the forest track north-east onto the plateau; park at the clearing by the cistern.
notes: High plateau Scots pine that fruits after the first cold rains and draws weekend pickers from Reus and Tarragona.

name: Llaberia North
access: From Pratdip take the track that climbs north into the Llaberia range; park at the fold below the north face.
notes: The shady side of Llaberia holds dew late and rovellons appear after storm fronts roll in off the sea.

name: Sant Marc
access: From Pratdip take the lane up to the Sant Marc hermitage; park at the hermitage and walk the crest.
notes: Open Aleppo slopes near the hermitage fruit only after wet storms, but the walk is short and pleasant.

name: La Mussara Plateau
access: From Vilaplana take the road up to the abandoned village of La Mussara; park at the village ruins.
notes: The famous plateau gets heavy weekend pressure, so weekday visits are the only way to beat the Reus crowd.

name: Boscos de la Mussara
access: From La Mussara take the track that drops south-west into the dense pinewood; park where the track forks.
notes: Dense high forest that keeps moisture all season and still hides unpicked pockets far from the ruin paths.

name: La Febró Side
access: From La Mussara take the road towards La Febró; park at the bend by the picnic area and climb east.
notes: East-facing Scots pine towards La Febró gives steady October flushes with fewer pickers than the plateau itself.

name: Serra del Monestir
access: From Vilanova d'Escornalbou take the road up to the Escornalbou monastery; park at the monastery car park.
notes: Shady slopes under the old monastery hold moisture and visitors pick the easy rings near the road first.

name: Serra d'Escornalbou
access: From Vilanova d'Escornalbou take the track along the serra crest; park at the bend by the dry-stone wall.
notes: Open south-east ground on the serra gives quick storm-triggered flushes and a short, busy season.

name: Llaberia de Colldejou
access: From Colldejou take the track that climbs into the Llaberia range; park at the fold where the pines close in.
notes: The high shady side of Llaberia keeps damp after sea storms and is barely picked outside the village.

name: Coll de Colldejou
access: From Colldejou take the lane towards the southern col; park at the col by the track junction.
notes: Sun-baked southern pines fruit only after real autumn storms, and the flush rarely lasts more than a week.
